question_name: Report your jurisdiction's most significant examples of collaboration with government, business, and/or civil society on climate-related issues.
response_answer: With the Government of Delhi actively seeking solutions to air quality and environment, GNCTD had established a program management unit with the Energy Policy Institute at the University of Chicago Trust in India (EPIC India at UCT) to incorporate an evidence-based approach to guide policy decisions and coordinate institutional efforts on improving the air quality of the National Capital Territory.  The team provides continuous support in designing and implementing evidence-based policies for cleaning Delhi’s air. The Department has collaborated with Reap Benefit India in its bid to engage the citizens of Delhi in climate action - Paryavaran Mitra. The initiative was launched on 7th July 2022 to create a network of people from Delhi, who have the awareness, knowledge, commitment, and potential to meet the challenges of environmental sustainability in their own spheres of influence. The programme aims to provide an opportunity to citizens for demonstrating environmental citizenship qualities through positive change in behaviour and action at individual, institutional, family and community levels through encouraging volunteerism in the environmental field.Delhi Solar Policy was first introduced in 2016 and to boost green energy and promote rooftop solar plants in residential areas in Delhi, the Delhi government recently signed a partnership with RMI to develop a new Delhi Solar Policy. The policy will position Delhi as a national and global leader in rooftop solar generation and has been envisaged with the objective of increasing the installed capacity of rooftop solar plants so that they can fulfil 10% of Delhi’s annual energy demand. The plan will also contribute to the creation of 40,000 new green jobs in this sector.For reducing water pollution from industrial effluents, industries operating in various industrial areas, have installed ETPs to meet the prescribed standards. Action is taken by Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) against the units, which are found operating in violation of the pollution control laws. More than 1400 units have installed Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs) to treat their effluents. The Delhi government and Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI) partnered in 2019 to host the Urban Mobility Lab- a platform that supports Indian cities in identifying, integrating, implementing, and scaling mobility solutions that transform how people and goods move. The initiative was aimed at translating policy action, developed by Delhi Government under the draft Electric Vehicles (EV) Policy, into on-ground development.WRI India entered into an agreement with the Public Works Department of the Delhi Government to set up a Technical Support Unit for the 540-km street redesign project in the national capital.  The street redesign project focuses on: Reducing traffic bottlenecks, increasing green cover, improving the efficiency of the existing space on roads, creating planned spaces for vehicles and making adequate space available for pedestrians and non-motorised transport users.Apart from these, the Department is engaged with multiple organisations from various sectors on a number of projects.

response_answer: Le projet vise à mettre en place un système d'éclairage public qui comprendra (i) la modernisation des appareilsd'éclairage existants ainsi que (ii) l'installation complète de nouveaux appareils d'éclairage et de lampes.Il s’agira d’un réseau mixte composé de lampadaires alimentés par l'énergie conventionnelle du réseauélectrique national et de certains alimentés par les énergies renouvelables.Un système de gestion centralisée, servira de point d'ancrage du réseau, garantissant le contrôle et la gestionà distance des lampadaires.Le système disposera de fonctions télécommandées qui permettent la gradation dynamique, l'ajustement et ladétection des pannes, l'allumage et l'extinction automatiques le soir et à l'aube, ainsi qu'une infrastructure de mesure avancée de la consommation d'énergie.Principaux impacts attendus Système de gestion à distance Suivi en temps réel de la consommation Réduction de la facture énergétique de 50% Réduction des frais de maintenance Meilleure durée de vie (12 – 15 ans) Meilleure sécurité des biens et des personnes Réduction de la « pollution lumineuse » Confort et qualité de vie Expérience et marketing urbainUn système non optimisé face à une demande croissante Dans la ville de Douala, l'éclairage public présente un certain nombre de déficiences tant au niveau du matériel d’éclairage, assez obsolète, que de l’organisation des opérations de maintenance. La consommation d’électricité de l’installation est jugée excessive au regard du service rendu, insuffisant pour une métropole qui estégalement le centre économique national.La Communauté Urbaine de Douala (« CUD ») souhaite moderniser son installation existante en améliorant ses performances (baisse de consommation électrique) et en réduisant les coûts de gestion et de maintenance (réduction des pannes, simplification de la maintenance). Une gestion non intelligente pour une métropole dynamique Le système actuel ne permet pas une gestion intégrée des infrastructures d’éclairage public, en l’absence d’une interconnexion de ses composants. Cette absence d’interconnexion rend la gestion inefficiente, limite la mesure transparente des consommations, la planification des maintenances, l’identification des fraudes et enfin accroît la charge financière globale du système.

question_name: Provide information on your jurisdiction’s oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities and how these issues have impacted your jurisdiction's planning.
column_name: Provide further details on your jurisdiction's oversight of climate-related issues
response_answer: In order to combat climate change and reduce the urban emissions in the city officially, the municipality has signed  Covenant of Mayors, CoM in 2013 under the coordination of Foreign Affairs. In 2020, the Climate Change and Clean Energy department was established with the approval of municipality parliament to collect all of the climate change mitigation and adaptation projects.  The department created Sustainable Energy Action Plan (SEAP) to control the energy consumption and develop renewable energy usage in the city in 2019. The SEAP process has been prepared in accordance with the CoM methodology used by all cities preparing a Sustainable Energy Action Plan. The following basic steps were followed in the process carried out in accordance with CoM's SEAP reporting template and accompanying method report: a) Preparing the greenhouse gas emission inventory and evaluating the current situation, b) Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by at least 40% in 2030 compared to the base year of 2019, c) Establishing sustainable energy actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Antalya Sustainable Energy Action Plan creates a roadmap for reducing emissions from energy consumption in different sectors determined with the participation of urban stakeholders. This roadmap was also started with the calculation of the current status greenhouse gas emissions inventory of the province of Antalya for 2019.  Antalya Metropolitan Municipality is  the first metropolitan municipality in Turkey to prepare the Sustainable Energy Action Plan Report by adopting the fight against climate change. The municipality also continued to carry out and disseminate exemplary practices in many areas such as landscaping, agriculture, transportation, energy management, environmental health, water management, marine pollution and control, environmental education and awareness-raising throughout the city. The municipality also prepared SECAP - Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan, as a result of long and detailed studies, that will provide guidance for our Antalya's goal of becoming a climate-friendly city.  Antalya Metropolitan Municipality still continued to carry out not short-term, day-saving projects, but planned, rule-based, technique and science-based continuous environmental projects that take into account the rights of future generations, with a city vision and common sense. The 18 environmental awards  have been received at local, national and international level during our tenure with the projects and practices. It is started this endeavour with the Municipality in the efforts to become a neutral carbon city for climate-friendly Antalya. With the works such as renewable energy usage  and energy efficiency in the service building Antalya Metropolitan Municipality placed as the first municipality and even the first official institution to receive the Climate Friendly Organization Certificate issued by TSE. Besides, this department was improved as the directorate titled as "Climate Change and Zero Waste" in 2022.

response_answer: The impact of budgetary capacity on Can Tho City's ability to adapt to climate change can challenge its adaptation efforts as follows:- Limited financial resources: Can Tho City may face constraints in terms of limited financial resources, competing priorities, and budgetary constraints. Insufficient funding can hinder the implementation of comprehensive climate change adaptation plans and limit the city's ability to invest in critical infrastructure, research, and capacity-building initiatives.- Uncertain and unpredictable funding streams: Climate change adaptation funding can be uncertain, irregular, or project-specific, making long-term planning and implementation challenging. Inadequate and unpredictable funding streams can hinder the city's ability to develop and sustain adaptation projects, leading to fragmented or incomplete efforts.- Cost of adaptation measures: Some climate change adaptation measures, such as building climate-resilient infrastructure or implementing advanced technology solutions, can involve substantial costs. If the budgetary capacity is limited, it can pose challenges in financing such measures, potentially slowing down or compromising the effectiveness of adaptation efforts.

question_name: Report details on the other climate-related plans, policies and/or strategies in your jurisdiction.
response_answer: The "New Taipei City Climate Change Response Action Autonomy Ordinance (Draft)", which will serve as the basis for New Taipei City to promote net-zero transformation in the future, is being drafted and is expected to be submitted to the parliament for review in 2022. The city government proposed four general principles including "integrated governance and flexible operation", "climate fund premium subsidy", "green financial investment market" and "giving consideration to both fair transformation and development" when formulating the self-governance regulations.“Integrated governance and flexible operation” means that the formulation of provisions is task-oriented by first taking stock of important transformation promotion projects, and then splitting them into authorities. If there is any uncertainty, the measures shall be specified in the article, but the promotion schedule, responsibilities and regions can be decided according to the subsequent scientific evaluation. "Climate fund premium subsidy" provides a legal basis for the management of the future central allocation of local carbon fees and donations made by enterprises that fail to achieve carbon neutrality; in the future, a transparent application supervision mechanism can be established to support the transformation application by communities, campuses, households and enterprises. "Green financial investment market" encourages the information disclosure of a certain scale of listed and OTC companies in New Taipei City and guides the market towards an environment-friendly model. "Giving consideration to both fair transformation and development" refers to the clear stipulation of fair transformation as one of the purposes of the climate fund in the ordinance, and behavior change is expressly defined as an important incentive measure in the future.The important chapters of the current draft cover six major areas including urban and rural adjustment, building energy conservation and efficiency improvement, circular economy and utilization, energy and industrial innovation, smart green transportation, and zero-carbon education and life promotion. In addition, there are general provisions, penalties, and supplementary chapters, which lay a good foundation for the scope, definition and legal tools of promotion.

question_name: Report the percentage of households within the jurisdiction with access to clean cooking fuels and technologies.
response_answer: Most households, restaurants, and institutions within New Taipei City use natural gas or liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) as the primary fuel for gas stoves.In terms of natural gas, according to statistics from the Ministry of Economic Affairs' Bureau of Energy, the natural gas penetration rate in New Taipei City was 63.93% in 2022. Additionally, based on statistics from the Bureau of Energy, the LPG penetration rate in 2021 was 35.36%. Therefore, it is estimated that over 99% of households have access to clean cooking fuels and technologies.In addition to gas stoves, people may also use electricity as a cooking energy source. The supply of electricity in Taiwan is coordinated and distributed by the state-owned enterprise Taiwan Power Company (Taipower), ensuring accessibility to energy for the population. According to Taipower's 2021 Sustainable Development Goals Report, except for restrictions imposed by laws and regulations, Taipower provides electricity services with a 100% application fulfillment rate. Almost all households within the jurisdiction have access to electricity, with the exception of a few low-income households.

response_answer: In 2019, New Taipei City issued Taiwan's first Voluntary Local Review (VLR). Despite the impact of the pandemic, the city remained committed to the spirit of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by "Leaving no one behind" and fulfilling the Mayor's commitment to the well-being and prosperity of its citizens. In 2021, the city released its second VLR, which includes 60 SDGs projects for New Taipei City. question_name: Describe the outcomes of the most significant adaptation actions your jurisdiction is currently undertaking. Note that this can include those in the planning and/or implementation phase.
column_name: Action description and web link to further information^
response_answer: The actions include the following plans:- Intelligent disaster prevention and water control systemEffectively grasp water status information, expedite early warning and judgment of disaster, integrate intelligent disaster prevention and water control system, immediately provide people with disaster mitigation and refuge, and take corresponding actions in advance, so as to play the effect of disaster prevention, disaster mitigation, and disaster reduction, in the face of global climate change and extreme weather change.- Hillside management and monitoring planMonitor hillside variations with satellites.- Governance of the whole river basin to protect the safety of the homelandGovern river drainage and wild streams, dredge river drainage and wild streams, and conserve and govern hillsides- Strengthening the flood drainage capacity of the metropolitan area and reduce flooding pointsImprove the drainage bottlenecks within the jurisdiction of the city, and give priority to the deployment of rainwater sewers in areas prone to flooding, so as to facilitate the completeness of urban drainage.- Project for deploying flood detention facilities   Introduce floodwater that exceeds the flood discharge standard for aqueduct, based on the existing space or via acquisition of construction lands, in flood-prone areas within the jurisdiction of Taoyuan City, and use the space/ land as a flood detention pond to protect the lives, bodies, and property of surrounding residents.- Handling road-side ditch dredging services1. Handle road-side ditch dredging services routinely, or as petitioned or notified in various districts of the city.2. Strengthen inspections and road-side ditch dredging services in flood-prone areas, during the flood prevention season, pre- and post-typhoon period, and after heavy rainfall,- Phase III Plan for furthering disaster prevention and reliefEnhance the disaster prevention and relief capabilities of the city government, strengthen the efficiency in disaster prevention and relief system and operations of district offices, so as to enable disaster prevention and relief work to take root from the grassroots.- Plan for promoting self-flood disaster prevention in communities  Incorporate the city's climate change scenarios and future climate impacts into the relevant training and guidance of the plan for promoting self-flood disaster prevention in communities, based on community grassroots, with the integration of internal and external resources of the community.Promote the knowledge of disaster prevention in the community, stimulate the public’ disaster prevention awareness, establish and plant the concept of national disaster prevention, and elevate the energy of disaster prevention, through the learning of knowledge and technologies related to disaster prevention and relief, so as to reduce the impact of flood disasters on people's living.- Education, training, and publicity on mudslide disaster prevention Conduct education, training, and publicity on mudslide disaster prevention for city residents in the stream areas facing potential mudslide, so as to reach the effect of early evacuation prior to the occurrence of disasters. The city government and district offices are to jointly handle the education, training, and publicity prior to the flood season, so as to enhance the disaster prevention capacity of residents in the hillside area of the city.- Implementation of the “Project for deploying disaster-prevention campus in schools below senior-high level" under the cooperation with Ministry of Education- Development of refuge shelter adjustment plan

Building upon the report, the city government formulated the "2020-2022 Taoyuan City Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan" in 2019.Although the name of the report includes ”Air Pollution”, the report is completely focused on climate risk and vulnerability assessment.

As a city situated in the Mekong Delta region, Can Tho is particularly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, such as sea-level rise, flooding, and salinization. Consequently, the city has made significant efforts to enhance its oversight of climate-related issues and implement sustainable practices. Here are some key aspects of Can Tho City's oversight:1. Climate Change Coordination Board: Can Tho City has established a Climate Change Coordination Board to facilitate collaboration and coordination among various government agencies, departments, and organizations. This board plays a vital role in formulating strategies, policies, and action plans to address climate change challenges in the city.2. Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation Plan: The city has developed a comprehensive Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation Plan, which outlines strategies and measures to minimize vulnerabilities and enhance resilience. This plan covers various sectors, including urban planning, agriculture, water management, infrastructure development, and public health.3. Flood and Salinity Control: Can Tho City faces recurrent flooding and salinity intrusion due to rising sea levels and upstream dam operations. To address these challenges, the city has invested in infrastructure projects such as the construction and improvement of flood control systems, dykes, and sluice gates. These measures help manage water levels and minimize the impact of flooding and salinity on agriculture and residents.4. Sustainable Urban Development: Can Tho City emphasizes sustainable urban development practices to mitigate the effects of climate change. The city promotes green infrastructure, including the incorporation of parks, green spaces, and rooftop gardens into urban planning. Additionally, Can Tho encourages the use of renewable energy sources, such as solar power, and promotes energy-efficient buildings.5. Public Awareness and Education: Can Tho City recognizes the importance of public awareness and education in addressing climate-related issues. The city organizes campaigns, workshops, and seminars to educate the public, raise awareness about climate change impacts, and promote sustainable practices at the individual and community levels.6. International Cooperation: Can Tho City actively engages in international cooperation and partnerships to access technical expertise, resources, and funding for climate change initiatives. The city collaborates with international organizations, non-governmental organizations, and other cities to share knowledge, experiences, and best practices in climate change adaptation and mitigation.These efforts demonstrate Can Tho City's commitment to effectively oversee and respond to climate-related challenges. By integrating climate change considerations into its policies, plans, and actions, Can Tho aims to build a more resilient and sustainable city for its residents.

response_answer: This report sets out the targets determined with the participation of the stakeholders of Antalya province and aimed at reducing emissions from energy consumption and greenhouse gases in different sectors. The most important bases of this report, the starting point of which is the Antalya province-scale greenhouse gas inventory, are the reports prepared or commissioned by Antalya Metropolitan Municipality and different institutions regarding the future of Antalya province, and the visions of the city stakeholders for the future of the city. In the preparation of the baseline Emissions Inventory, the activity-based approach most commonly used by cities was used. In this approach, all CO2e (or GHG) emissions from direct (through fuel combustion) or indirect (through electricity consumption) energy consumption in Antalya are included. Most GHG emissions are CO2 emissions, while CH4 and N2O emissions are of secondary importance for combustion processes in the residential and transportation sectors. All CO2, CH4 and CO2 emissions are calculated for all fuel types along with their global warming potential (GWP) using IPCC emission factors from the Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). One of the reasons for including emissions other than CO2 is that Antalya calculates emissions from waste (CH4), wastewater (CH4, N2O), enteric fermentation of livestock (CH4) and chemical fertilizers used in agriculture (N2O).

response_answer: "Roda Hijau" translates to "Green Wheel" in English. The term "roda" means "wheel" or "circle," which symbolizes constant movement, while "hijau" means "green," representing the lush and natural aspect. Combining these meanings, "Green Wheel" refers to a constantly moving entity dedicated to making the city of Medan greener and managing waste effectively.The birth of the Green Wheel community was inspired by Christella Suwongso, the initiator of the community, who was deeply concerned about the waste issue in Medan. During her engineering studies in environmental technology, she realized that the waste problem in Medan was more profound than just the presence of waste. It required the active involvement of society, the government, the implementation of appropriate technologies, and funding support.Green Wheel collaborates with the Medan City Government to enhance waste reduction programs at the household level. Through their efforts, they aim to reduce the overall waste generation in the city by up to 10% annually.

response_answer: Taoyuan City will join the Alliance of Decoalizers in 2023, and is phasing out coal burning in 2030. In the future, 60% Solid Recovered Fuels (SRF, wood pellets, and etc.) and 40% natural gas or electricity will be used as an alternative to coal burning. In response to the replacement of coal burning, the demand for SRF will increase. The huge waste produced in Taoyuan City is as high as 20,000 metric tons per year. To properly handle the huge waste in Taoyuan City, it is planned to build a waste MT demonstration center in Dayuan District of Taoyuan City, which utilizes huge waste to produce SRF as an alternative fuel for boilers, achieving a diversified way of transforming waste into biomass energy.Taoyuan City is an important manufacturing center in Taiwan, with an annual output of about 346,000 metric tons of industrial waste with high calorific value suitable for SRF. It has now guided the establishment of 7 SRF manufacturing and usage factories; totally produced 50,000 metric tons of SRF (code: 170044) in 2022. The consuming factories of SRF (code: 170044) consumed 85,000 metric tons of SRF, which is the top one in Taiwan. It is expected that by 2030, eight high-calorific-value SRF processing, recycling and consuming institutions will be established with a consumption amount of 150,000 metric tons per year.

response_answer: A current situation release inventory was prepared by using the data of Antalya Metropolitan Municipality for 2019. During the preparation of the Sustainable Energy Action Plan, the short and long term strategic plans of the Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, the opinions of academicians, chambers of industry and commerce, public institutions, provincial directorates and professional organizations were taken into consideration. For 2019, the energy consumption of Antalya including industry is calculated as 28.623.531 MWh and greenhouse gas emission as 10.683.551 tCO2e.The share of emissions from fuel and electricity consumption of buildings in total emissions is 47.1%. Greenhouse gas emissions from transportation are 30.2%. Greenhouse gas emissions from solid waste and wastewater treatment are 8.2%, while the rate of emissions from electricity generation is 8.5% and emissions from agriculture and livestock are around 6%.  The energy consumption of Antalya excluding industry is calculated as 21.493.229 MWh and the total amount of greenhouse gas emissions is 8.232.919 tCO2e. According to calculations, 53.1% is buildings, 36.3% is transportation, and 10.6% is solid waste and other emissions from wastewater emissions.

question_name: Report your jurisdiction’s main adaptation goals.
response_answer: Climate change and urbanization pressure lead to the deterioration of ecosystems, causing damage to both natural areas and people. Especially in Antalya, which is one of the leading cities in terms of ecosystem richness, the demand for new settlement areas created by the rapidly increasing population after the 1980s has led to the shrinkage of natural areas and the growth of artificial areas. Consequently, the artificial boundaries of the city have expanded, resulting in the destruction of ecosystems. In addition, climate change, which has been increasing in recent years, causes extremely negative impacts on ecosystems. Ecosystem degradation is both caused by climate change and increases the effects of climate change. Therefore, restoration of ecosystems in Antalya is extremely important. In order to carry out ecosystem restoration, the city's ecosystems should be monitored periodically with various digital tools (such as using databases obtained from satellite images and creating new GIS-based data sets), degradation should be detected and methods to prevent degradation should be applied by expert teams.

column_name: Describe how climate-related issues have impacted your jurisdiction's financial planning
response_answer: There are two sub-steps in the Metropolitan Municipality's financial planning for the management of climate-related issues. The first one is funds, grants and loans from national sources. The existing budget and national resources of Metropolitan Municipalities are not sufficient for the development and implementation of climate-related projects. Therefore, there is also a need for international support (World Bank, ICLE, Covenant of Mayors, UNDP, etc.). The budgets created with the support received shape the financial steps that Antalya will take in combating and adapting to climate change, especially in the face of floods, heat waves and public health problems caused by climate change. Here, knowing that not only the methods to be applied as a municipality, but also the financial supports, political decisions and steps are also important guides us on how to direct project financing resources. If financial resources are directed correctly, costs up to 10 times the budget to be spent before the disaster will be avoided.

response_answer: Antalya is the 5th most populous city in Turkey with a rapidly growing population and continuous migration. With increasing population and urbanization, inadequate urban infrastructure and lack of sufficient budget cause great difficulty in the transition to a low-carbon economy. In addition, although the education level of the people is around average, they are often weak in terms of awareness. The budget problems of municipalities with the central government, exchange rate differences and increasing inflation also negatively affect Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, just like the municipalities in our country. An important problem is that the infrastructure needed for the transition to a low carbon economy is not domestically produced and this creates difficulties due to the exchange rate.

response_answer: Regarding the phenomena and trends of climate change, as assessed in IPCC AR6, the estimated global surface warming caused by human activities from 1850-1900 to 2010-2019 is 1.07°C (0.8°C-1.3°C). Various greenhouse gases are responsible for approximately 1.0°C-2.0°C of warming, while other human-driven factors such as aerosols have led to a cooling effect of 0-0.8°C. Natural drivers have influenced surface temperature changes within the range of -0.1°C to +0.1°C. Climate change, such as extreme heat, has impacts on the emergence of new types of diseases, which may pose challenges for timely responses by certain medical institutions and organizations in specific regions.New forms of diseases are affected by climate change (e.g., extreme high temperatures) and can lead to a variety of patterns that may not be addressed in a timely manner by medical institutions and units in some areas. As the proportion of the elderly population in New Taipei City continues to rise, without considering the need to improve adaptability, the proportion of elderly populations in some areas is high and medical institutions are inadequate.According to the "New Taipei City Climate Change Adaption Plan", the heat island temperature in Sanchong District, Luzhou District, Zhonghe District, Yonghe District and Xindian District has increased significantly, and the population of these five administrative districts accounts for about 30-40% of the city's population.

response_answer: The actions include the following plans:- Formulate the four major functional zoning maps of the city's national land planIn accordance with the provisions of the Land Law, research and develop the city's land plan, including space development and growth management plan, planning and adjustment of land functional zoning and classification, principles of land use control, departmental space development plan, climate change adaptation plan etc.- Formulation of the four major functional zoning maps of the city's national land plan Develop the city's national land plan in accordance with the provisions of the Spatial Planning Act, including contents such as space development, growth management plan, and planning/ design/ adjustment/ land control principles for the zoning and classification of national land by functions, departmental space development plans, climate change adjustment plan, etc. - Conduct hierarchical management of the large-scale hillside communities, based on the objective monitoring data collected for hillside communities.- Study and review of the standard for classifying the availability limit of hillside landsConfirm whether those lands, temporarily undesignated land within the scope of hillside lands, are suitable for agriculture and forestry as per the classification of availability limits, which can be used as a reference basis for land administration agencies during land designation.- Basic survey plan for important wetlandsHandle the wetland basic survey plan and establish wetland ecological data.- Conducting outflow control for lands with a development area of more than 2 hectares and in a legal development stateRequest any proposed outflow control plans to include mandatory assessments of impacts on bases and regions under the impact of future climate change, and adopt outflow control schemes with low-impact development concept or with addition of flood detention space, etc., according to topographical characteristics of the base.- In terms of urban renewal development planning, those who make contributions to the acquisition of green building labels and overall planning and design will be rewarded for floor area-related update, with the approval through deliberation.

question_name: Report on your engagement with other levels of government regarding your jurisdiction's climate action.
response_answer: Since 2014, the central government (The Environmental Protection Administration) has been working with city governments to encourage villages to participate in the "Certification Program for Low Carbon Sustainable Homeland" to build the capacity of residents to take action to mitigate and adapt to climate change and to live a low-carbon lifestyle.  This certification can raise the awareness of environmental protection and the concept of energy saving and carbon reduction, accumulate the outcomes from bottom to top, and guide residents to implement a low carbon lifestyle from top to bottom.A number of low-carbon sustainability initiatives in New Taipei City are working well, such as phasing out indoor lighting, protecting wetlands and urban ponds, storing and reusing rainwater, promoting community gardens, and encouraging wall plantings or green hedges, etc. These initiatives are being replicated in New Taipei City to achieve the goal of full implementation.1. Policy PromotionIn conjunction with the "low-carbon sustainable Homeland" promoted by the Environmental Protection Administration of the central government, New Taipei City is encouraging schools to adopt low-carbon measures. In addition, low-carbon facilities in public areas such as activity centers, state-owned land, libraries, parks, etc. are being renovated to enhance the overall benefits of energy saving and environmental protection and to establish a low-carbon lifestyle in New Taipei City.2. Setting up a project teamIn addition to the staff of relevant departments, experts and scholars from both industry and academia are also invited to join the task force to provide professional advice and suggestions on climate actions and policies. 3. Establish demonstration sites and counseling and subsidy mechanism(1) Low Carbon CommunityMost of the energy saving and carbon reduction measures in apartment building communities start with the replacement of lighting facilities. People are rarely aware that carbon reduction can also be carried out by water saving, resource recycling, green transport use, building shell insulation, and education.(2) Conduct home-based power-saving diagnosing and counseling  New Taipei City forms an expert team "The Power Doctors" to provide free power-saving diagnosing and counseling services. This service is provided to communities, institutions, and schools. And the given suggestions include energy saving in facilities such as air conditioning and lighting systems, water management, recycling and greening and heat insulation of buildings, etc. (3) Low Carbon CampusTo promote low-carbon concepts through school education, New Taipei City established the first "Low Carbon School Certification" system in 2009. In 2013, New Taipei City launched the “Little Environmental Leader” project, encouraging schools to establish student self-governing organizations and develop school-wide environmental protection courses through the “Little Environmental Leader” project, and subsidies schools in renovating energy-inefficient facilities to create a low-carbon campus. It takes into account 6 factors in "Low Carbon School Certification": green building, green energy, recycling, green transportation, sustainable environment, and innovative actions.(4) Since 2010, the central government (The Environmental Protection Administration) initiated the “Low Carbon Sustainable Homeland" project, started the "Certification Program for Low Carbon Sustainable Homeland ", and promoted the "Low Carbon Sustainable Home Certification and Rating Program" to promote low-carbon. The New Taipei City environmental protection department also supports villages in renovating facilities to get the certifications. There is a total of 512 villages are currently participating in the project so far. And New Taipei City is also the first city to receive the highest level of certification.4. Establishment of regional low carbon promotion centers(1) New Taipei City established the " Low Carbon Promotion Center", which organized courses and workshops on energy saving and carbon reduction for citizens, and provides the city's environmental protection policies and environmental education. The courses include roof farm construction, reuse of household waste, urban home greening, etc. Through environmental education, we hope to promote a low-carbon lifestyle to the general community, neighborhoods, and households. (2) New Taipei City government trained “Low Carbon Community Planners”, which is a professional team that provides services for the planning of energy-efficient renovations of communities.

question_name: Report how your jurisdiction assesses the wider environmental, social, and economic opportunities and benefits of climate action.
column_name: Outline how your jurisdiction quantifies the equitable and inclusive distribution of climate action
response_answer: To quantify the equitable and inclusive distribution of climate action in Can Tho City, several approaches have been adopted to ensure that the benefits and burdens of climate action are shared fairly among different social groups as shown below:1. Data collection and analysis:- Collect data on demographics, socio-economic indicators, vulnerability assessments, and climate-related risks at the local level. This includes information on income levels, education, gender, ethnicity, and other relevant social factors.- Analyze the data to identify existing disparities and inequalities in access to resources, services, and opportunities related to climate action.- Consider intersectional perspectives, acknowledging that individuals may belong to multiple disadvantaged groups, and analyze the unique challenges they face.2. Stakeholder engagement and participation:- Engage with a diverse range of stakeholders, including community representatives, civil society organizations, marginalized groups, and vulnerable communities, to understand their perspectives, needs, and priorities.- Establish mechanisms for meaningful participation, such as public consultations, community workshops, and inclusive decision-making processes, to ensure that the voices of marginalized groups are heard and their perspectives are considered.3. Equity and social justice assessment:- Conduct an equity assessment of climate action measures and policies to evaluate their potential distributional impacts.- Assess the differential impacts of climate action on different social groups, considering factors such as income, gender, age, disability, and geographic location.- Examine the accessibility, affordability, and availability of climate-related services, such as renewable energy, adaptation infrastructure, healthcare, and social protection programs.4. Indicators and metrics:- Develop indicators and metrics that can quantitatively measure the equitable distribution of climate action. These indicators capture the distribution of benefits, access to services, participation in decision-making, and overall well-being of different social groups.- Examples of indicators include the percentage of low-income households with access to renewable energy, the number of women in leadership roles in climate-related initiatives, and the availability of climate-resilient infrastructure in vulnerable areas.5. Monitoring and evaluation:- Regularly monitor and evaluate the implementation of climate action measures to assess their impacts on equity and inclusiveness.- Use the established indicators and metrics to track progress, identify gaps, and make necessary adjustments to ensure equitable outcomes.Integrate feedback from stakeholders, marginalized groups, and local communities into the monitoring and evaluation processes to ensure that their concerns and needs are considered.6. Reporting and transparency:- Publish reports and communicate the findings of the equitable distribution assessment to promote transparency and accountability.- Share the results with stakeholders, policymakers, and the public to foster awareness, understanding, and support for inclusive climate action.- Use the findings to inform policy and decision-making processes, ensuring that climate action strategies and programs prioritize equitable and inclusive outcomes.By adopting these steps, Can Tho City quantified and monitored the equitable and inclusive distribution of climate action, allowing for targeted interventions and policies that address the specific needs of marginalized groups and ensure that the benefits of climate action reach all sections of society.

question_name: Report details on the climate action plan or strategy that addresses mitigation, adaptation (resilience), and/or energy-related issues in your jurisdiction.
column_name: Describe if and how climate-related scenarios have informed the plan
response_answer: Can Tho City has taken climate-related scenarios into account in its action plan on climate change. These scenarios provide valuable information about potential future climate conditions, enabling the city to better understand the risks and challenges it may face. By incorporating climate-related scenarios into the action plan, Can Tho City can develop strategies and measures that are responsive and adaptable to different climate change scenarios.The action plan of Can Tho City on climate change considered various climate-related scenarios, such as changes in temperature, rainfall patterns, sea-level rise, and extreme weather events. These scenarios help identify vulnerable areas, sectors, and populations within the city and guide decision-making processes to prioritize adaptation and mitigation efforts.Based on the climate-related scenarios, the action plan outlined specific actions and measures to address the identified risks and challenges. This included improving infrastructure resilience, implementing flood control measures, promoting sustainable agricultural practices, enhancing water resource management, adopting renewable energy solutions, and enhancing public awareness and capacity building.The incorporation of climate-related scenarios into the action plan demonstrates Can Tho City's proactive approach to climate change adaptation and mitigation. By considering various future climate scenarios, the city can make informed decisions, prioritize resources effectively, and take appropriate actions to build resilience and sustainability in the face of climate change.

reporting_authority: CDP Cities; ICLEI - Local Governments for Sustainability; Global Covenant of Mayors
question_name: Describe the outcomes of the most significant mitigation actions your jurisdiction is currently undertaking. Note that this can include those in the planning and/or implementation phases.
column_name: Action description and web link to further information^
response_answer: Since joining the Powering Past Coal Alliance in 2020, Kaohsiung City has implemented a series of coal reduction policies. These include measures such as reducing the operation of units at the Hsinta Power Plant during the autumn and winter seasons and extending the coal reduction period by 30 days. The city has also required and provided guidance to cogeneration plants to gradually reduce coal consumption.In 2021, Kaohsiung City achieved a cumulative coal reduction of 1.79 million metric tons, which further increased to 2.19 million metric tons in 2022. The city has set a target of 3.4 million metric tons of coal reduction for cogeneration plants by 2025 and a complete cessation of coal consumption of 3.85 million metric tons at the Hsinta Power Plant.In addition to coal reduction efforts, the Hsinta Power Plant has initiated a demonstration project for mixed hydrogen power generation using gas turbines. The project broke ground in February this year, aiming to achieve a hydrogen blend of 5% by 2025, gradually transitioning towards a low-carbon power generation structure.

question_name: Provide details on your climate risk and vulnerability assessment.
response_answer: Women and children, ethnic minorities, and the elderly are the most vulnerable to these effects. O Mon, Co Do, Phong Dien, and Thoi Lai districts are predicted to have the highest vulnerability to climate change impacts among the nine districts and should therefore be prioritized for adaptive investments, such as increasing the area of green spaces, building water-storage areas, combining floodplains and wetland parks, preserving biodiversity and planning for biodiversity conservation to improve environmental resilience. In summary, the pilot calculations described here show that the indicator set used provides an intuitive view, facilitating managers to easily delineate those areas with the highest vulnerability and in greatest need of investment. The set of indicators used is also highly applicable because most of the input data are collected from the local Statistical Yearbook published annually. Therefore, this set of indicators could be scaled up for other cities/provinces in Vietnam and undergo continuous improvement.

response_answer: The smart and Energy Efficient City Project (SEECP) was proposed by the Asian Development Bank to be implemented in 6 provinces/cities in Viet Nam, including Can Tho. The project aims to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions in Can Tho city in the long term, through creating a project roadmap as well as developing a smart city and energy-efficient infrastructure with LED lights and smart technology used for public lighting and public buildings. Furthermore, the project also promotes a favorable environment for efficient energy use, access to capital, capacity building, and awareness-raising.The smart lighting component of SEECP will help Can Tho to replace 30,579 current street lamps with LED lights, 747 old electrical cabinets or control panels with a control center integrated with intelligent devices, and 381 smart light poles. Besides, the project will also pilot the smart building model in 50 public buildings in Can Tho, including schools, offices, etc., with a connected load capacity greater than 600 kW. It is estimated that SEECP will reduce 6.5% of the total electricity consumption of Can Tho, hence contributing to a cutdown of 226,689 tCO2eq.

response_answer: The New Taipei City joined the Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) in 2019, becoming the first city in Taiwan to join the alliance, and announced that by the end of the year, it would complete two control policies, namely, "phasing out coal-fired boilers" and "replacing asphalt industry’s fuel from oil to gas", so as to reduce the average concentration of PM2.5 to less than 15 µg/m3 of air quality standards, and continue to promote the completion of the goal of "exit of coal-fired steam electricity symbiotic units" in 2022. Since 2023, the industries in the City will no longer use coal as fuel, and the City will also set reduction targets and promote various control measures for the continuous improvement of the City's air quality.The city completed the early retirement of its last coal-fired unit in October 2022, becoming the first in the country to achieve the goal of a coal-free city ahead of schedule, fulfilling its commitment as a member of the Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA).The annual average value of PM2.5 in the City is 12.4 µg/m3 in 2021. The annual average value of PM2.5 in the City is 10.5 µg/m3 in 2022. The annual average value of PM2.5 in the City aims to reach 12.0 µg/m3 . Since 2019, it has been lower than the national standard of 15 µg/m3 for three consecutive years, and the 24-hour average value is lower than 35 µg/m3. The target of PM10 annual average value is to reach 28.0 µg/m3 by 2023. At present, the latest index value (2021 annual average value) is 24.7 µg/m3.

Limited access to quality data and information can hinder the city's ability to assess climate risks and develop appropriate adaptation measures.- Financial constraints: Building technical capacity often requires financial resources for training, research, and the acquisition of technology and tools. Lack of collaboration among different sectors can hinder the city's ability to integrate technical expertise across disciplines for holistic climate change adaptation.

question_name: Report your jurisdiction's most significant examples of collaboration with government, business, and/or civil society on climate-related issues.
response_answer: To accelerate carbon reduction efforts and respond to the global trend, Kaohsiung City has established the "Net-Zero Industry Alliance." The alliance focuses on five major industries: steel, petrochemicals, electronics, energy, and circular economy. It includes companies that account for 70% of the industrial emissions in Kaohsiung.The tasks of the industry alliance include:1. Establish short, medium, and long-term goals based on the emission status and net-zero pathway planning for each team member.2. Provide annual reports on reduction plans and funding.3. Monitor the implementation progress through annual reporting of greenhouse gas emissions.4. Organize carbon reduction knowledge and technology sharing meetings annually, such as conducting workshops on "Product Carbon Footprint" with a focus on the petrochemical industry. Invite experts from the industry and research institutes to engage in practical discussions.To promote renewable energy, the "Green Energy Promotion Task Force" was established with a target of 1.25GW over a 6-year period. In terms of circular economy, efforts are made to integrate resources in industrial areas, such as sharing steam, waste heat, and industrial gases, to reduce energy consumption. Collaboration between the steel and petrochemical industries is also promoted, aiming to utilize the carbon dioxide generated from steelmaking as raw material for the petrochemical industry, thus achieving carbon dioxide circulation. In terms of industry assistance, Carbon Footprint Guidance Teams and Energy Efficiency Guidance Teams have been established, with experts and scholars visiting factories to assist businesses in conducting carbon footprint assessments and improving processes.https://reurl.cc/eDn3mW

response_answer: The New Taipei City Government has pioneered the establishment of the "Energy Saving Clinic Program," which brings together experts from various fields such as lighting, air conditioning, power systems, resource recycling, water-saving systems, and green buildings to form a diagnostic service team. The team provides professional energy-saving diagnosis services for residential buildings, office buildings, government agencies, schools, hospitals, stores, department stores, temples, and other buildings. They offer energy-saving recommendations and evaluate the improvement benefits and payback period. To encourage community energy-saving renovations, communities can submit low-carbon renovation applications through low-carbon planners trained by the New Taipei City Government. The government will provide funding to assist communities in carrying out renovations. Completed renovated communities can participate in the "Energy-Saving E-house" program, apply for the "New Taipei City Low-carbon Community Label," and participate in the evaluation of "Excellent Apartment Buildings in New Taipei City" to assess the effectiveness of energy-saving improvements.In 2030, New Taipei City will establish the "Building Energy Equipment Efficiency Standards" and the "Public Building Carbon Neutrality Standards" to achieve the goals of having newly constructed buildings meet the 1+ energy efficiency level by 2045, and 50% of existing buildings reach the 1+ energy efficiency level by 2050.

question_name: Provide details on your climate risk and vulnerability assessment.
response_answer: The assessment is conducted to understand the vulnerability and adaptive capacity of the poor community in Can Tho City. It aims to explore the relationship between determining factors of vulnerability and adaptive capacity of the poor community to climate change. The asessment seeks to provide a scientific basis for developing a comprehensive and sustainable strategic plan for Can Tho City, contributing to mitigation and adaptation to climate change. It adopts the Vulnerability and Adaptive Capacity Assessment (VACA) framework proposed by CARE as the research method.Through sociological surveys, the assessment analyzes information and calculates vulnerability indices using the formula proposed by the UNESCO-IHE Institute for Water Education and the weighting method by Iyengar-Sudarshan. The findings conclude that there is a significant need to enhance the adaptive capacity of the poor community in Can Tho City in the context of climate change impacts. It also proposes measures to improve the adaptive capacity of the poor community, including: (1) implementing long-term sustainable interventions to enhance community education, (2) establishing diverse and income-stable livelihood options, while adopting community-specific approaches for disseminating climate change information to the poor community, and (3) ensuring that rapidly developing areas do not leave behind the poor community, as they are particularly vulnerable and easily excluded from support programs.

question_name: Provide details of your jurisdiction's energy-related targets active in the reporting year. In addition, you can report other climate-related targets active in the reporting year.
response_answer: According to the “New Taipei City 2050 Net Zero Roadmap and Climate Action White Paper”, the target power generation of solar photovoltaic and geothermal power in New Taipei City in 2030 is 150 MW, of which the total installed capacity of solar photovoltaic needs to reach 140 MW in 2030, and the total installed capacity is 81.7 MW at present. In order to achieve the short-term goal, New Taipei City has set a target of increasing 10 MW per year. In the private sector, the development potential of industries and communities will be checked, solar photovoltaic systems and public solar photovoltaic public power plants will be set up in industrial zones, and a new renewable energy information system will be established in New Taipei City.Through the continuous handling of public field lease bidding, joint plant bidding for lease, incentives and subsidies, public and private sectors work together to expand renewable energy. It is expected that the solar photovoltaic power generation will reach 240 MW in 2040 and 340 MW in 2050. In addition, large energy consumers are defined in the autonomous regulations, and energy consumers with high power consumption are required to set up renewable energy and energy storage equipment in electric fields or appropriate places, or purchase a certain amount of renewable energy or certificates.In terms of forward-looking energy development, Jinshan geothermal demonstration site is to be set up with the goal of 10 MW geothermal power generation by 2030, and a biomass energy power plant is to be set up by 2030 to develop biogas power generation.

column_name: Describe the wider opportunities/benefits of climate action the jurisdiction has identified
response_answer: 1. Improve the quality of natural resources (e.g., air quality, water quality) and promote health benefits.New Taipei City has completed three key policies, including the "phasing out coal-fired boilers" and "replacing of asphalt industry’s fuel from oil to gas" in 2019 and the "phasing out coal-fired steam electricity symbiotic units" in 2022, which is expected to make New Taipei City a coal-free city from 2023. In addition, the city government has been integrating various resources. Through cross-departmental cooperation, New Taipei City has succeeded in decreasing PM2.5 concentrations in the jurisdiction through policies such as building a comprehensive public transportation system, expanding public bicycle system, promoting cleaner vehicles, and promoting the installation of continuous automatic air pollution monitoring facilities in factory boilers. In the future, we will move towards more strict air quality goals (annual average PM2.5 concentration below 10µg/m3 by 2030). In addition, policies such as waste management and the promotion of circular economy can reduce waste, improve water quality of rivers and reduce marine pollution.2. Green economy, and sharing economy, and promote green job opportunities.(1) Green Economy.A. New Taipei City started to replace traditional streetlights with LED lights in 2013, finished it in 2015, and started to replace the LED streetlights with more energy-efficient smart LED lights in 2020, which will not only reduce greenhouse gas emissions but also promote green jobs and enhance the competitiveness of green industries.B. New Taipei city's "food waste reducing restaurants" utilize ugly vegetables and fruits as ingredients to minimize waste.C. Green Store project, which promotes restaurants and supermarkets with less waste, aims at 4 major industries, which are fast food chains, retailing, supermarkets, and restaurants, and evaluates them for source reduction and waste minimization, food conservation, recycling, environment cleanliness, environmental education, and energy conservation. Pushing these major livelihood-related industries to operate in a more energy-efficient and waste-reducing way.(2) Sharing economy: Build a New Taipei City Public Bicycle System and promote shared scooter and car rental services, and encourage operators to provide services in the community.3. Enhancing Social EquityThe Food Sharing Network (donating surplus fruits and vegetables to the disadvantaged), and the Happiness Station (giving second-hand furniture and appliances to low-income households) are projects that share items with residents or social welfare organizations. In addition to minimizing waste, it can also provide care for vulnerable groups.4. More efficient land use patterns to facilitate people's livelihoodsNew Taipei City continuously expands its public transportation network, including MRT routes, transit buses, shared bikes, and pedestrian corridors. In addition, reducing greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions, it can also reduce the number of transfers for passengers, save travel time, and enhance the convenience of citizens' life. With a dense, comprehensive, mass transportation infrastructure, most of the public activities gather around the public transport station and achieve a high-quality transportation system and sustainable and efficient land use structure.

response_answer: Governments in Delhi have completed their five year terms for the most part. Political stability plays a crucial role in enhancing the adaptive capacity of Delhi in the face of environmental challenges, including climate change impacts. A stable political environment provides the foundation for effective governance, policy implementation, and long-term planning, all of which are essential for building resilience and responding to evolving climate-related threats. The current party that forms the government of NCT of Delhi has been in power since 2015 and is committed to addressing environmental issues in Delhi through various policies and initiatives. The party's manifesto emphasizes the importance of sustainability and pledges to reduce pollution, conserve water, and promote renewable energy.  The Electric Vehicle (EV) policy underscores the government's focus on sustainable mobility, aiming to reduce emissions and promote cleaner transportation options. This policy aligns with global trends towards electric vehicles, contributing to a reduction in air pollution and the city's carbon footprint.Similarly, the development of a solar policy highlights Delhi's ambition to harness renewable energy sources. By encouraging solar installations, the government seeks to diversify the energy mix, enhance energy security, and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.The "Delhi @2047" initiative exemplifies a long-term vision, emphasizing comprehensive planning for the city's sustainable development over the coming decades. This demonstrates a commitment to proactive governance that addresses environmental challenges and ensures a livable and resilient future for its residents. These policies and projects collectively showcase a commitment to sustainable development, cleaner technologies, and community well-being, which contribute to enhancing the city's adaptive capacity and fostering a greener and more prosperous future.

response_answer: In this study, emissions calculations for water transportation, such as sea vessels and fishing boats, were not performed separately. Instead, the fuel consumption for fishing boats was accounted for within the emissions calculations for land transportation.It is common in emission inventories to combine fuel consumption data for small-scale water transportation, like fishing boats, with land-based transportation activities due to their relatively smaller contribution to the overall emissions compared to larger vessels like ships. By doing so, the study can focus on the major sources of emissions while still considering the impact of smaller water transportation activities.This approach is often used when there is limited data availability or when the emissions from smaller water vessels are not expected to significantly impact the overall emission estimates for the area under study. However, it's essential to consider the specific context and scale of emissions from various transportation modes to develop comprehensive and accurate emission inventories and environmental assessments.

response_answer: The New Taipei City government plans to improve the user environment for electric vehicles, promote the installation of charging piles in residential, commercial and public parking spaces through regulations, and require new buildings to reserve space for charging piles, and public parking lots to have a certain percentage of charging piles. Exclusive parking spaces for electric vehicle charging, parking discounts and charging rate discounts are to be set through the management strategy of electric vehicles.In addition, the City will promote the electrification of private vehicles in the form of subsidies first and controls later, in conjunction with the control of air quality maintenance areas. By 2040, the market-to-sales ratio of electric motorcycles and locomotives is expected to reach 100%; by 2035, full electrification of motorcycles and touring buses in the logistics industry will be implemented, and the passage area for fuel motorcycles will be fully controlled; in 2040, the control of the passage area of fuel vehicles, passenger cars, and small trucks will be expanded, and the full electrification of cargo trucks in the logistics industry will be stipulated. response_answer: In 2023, the city of Medan and its surrounding areas will launch the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system with an initial budget allocation of Rp1.8 trillion. This project aims to enhance public transportation and address traffic congestion in the city. BRT is a high-capacity bus-based public transportation system that operates on dedicated lanes or separate roadways, allowing for faster and more efficient travel compared to traditional bus services.The government of North Sumatra Province, together with the local governments of Medan City, Binjai City, and Deliserdang Regency, has held preparatory meetings for the implementation of the BRT system. Additionally, the local governments of Medan, Binjai, and Deliserdang have signed a memorandum of cooperation for the planned operation of the BRT. BRT is an urban mass transportation mode that provides fast, comfortable, and cost-effective mobility. It has gained popularity in Jakarta, where it is known as the "busway."By launching the BRT system, it is expected to make public transportation in Medan and its surrounding areas more efficient, reducing travel time, and encouraging more people to use public transportation. Moreover, BRT can contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by decreasing the use of private vehicles, which are more prone to causing air and traffic pollution.

response_answer: Can Tho City relies heavily on water resources for agriculture, fisheries, and domestic use. Climate change affects water availability and quality, leading to challenges in water management. The city are investing in water infrastructure, such as reservoirs, canals, and irrigation systems, to ensure adequate water supply for different sectors. Financial planning is accounting for the costs of developing and maintaining water infrastructure, as well as implementing water conservation measures and promoting efficient water use practices. Water stress in Can Tho City can be exacerbated by climate change impacts:- Changes in Precipitation Patterns: Climate change can alter rainfall patterns, resulting in changes in the timing, intensity, and distribution of precipitation. This can lead to periods of drought or heavy rainfall, both of which can contribute to water stress in different ways.- Droughts: Reduced precipitation and prolonged dry periods can lead to water scarcity, affecting water availability for domestic, agricultural, and industrial purposes. Droughts can strain water resources, leading to water rationing and restrictions.- Sea-Level Rise and Saline Intrusion: Can Tho City is located in the Mekong Delta, which is vulnerable to sea-level rise. As sea levels rise, saltwater intrusion can occur, contaminating freshwater sources and reducing their availability for consumption and irrigation. Saline intrusion can lead to increased water stress, particularly for agriculture and communities dependent on freshwater sources.- Groundwater Depletion: Climate change impacts, such as increased temperatures and changes in precipitation patterns, can alter groundwater recharge rates. Over-extraction of groundwater for various purposes, including agriculture and urban water supply, combined with reduced recharge rates, can lead to groundwater depletion and increased water stress.

response_answer: The vast majority of urban areas are occupied by buildings, and since this cannot be changed, policies are being directed towards transforming them into net-zero green buildings. In 2020, the residential and commercial sectors in New Taipei City accounted for 39% of the city's carbon emissions. To reduce emissions in these sectors, three zero-carbon strategies - "energy monitoring," "energy retrofitting," and "carbon-free electricity" - along with public facility improvements and behavior changes will be promoted. The public sector will take the lead, followed by gradual implementation in the private sector. New constructions will adopt zero-carbon designs, which will then be extended to existing buildings, again with the public sector leading the way and eventually expanding to the private sector.By 2045, newly constructed buildings will comply with a minimum of Class 1 energy efficiency, and by 2050, 50% of existing buildings will achieve a minimum of Class 1 energy efficiency, thereby realizing the vision of nearly zero-energy buildings.

response_answer: Though the price of electricity in Taiwan is relatively low, there shouldn't be many energy-poor families. However, aqccording to the co-research from Industrial Technology Research Institute(ITRI) and Taiwan Fund for Children and Families, out of a total of 1,000 economically disadvantaged (low-income) households in Taiwan, 61% are affected by energy poverty. In response to this, Kaohsiung City participated in the "Residential and Commercial Electricity Saving Action Plan Jointly. Promoted by Counties and Cities" initiated by the central government in 2015, to address energy poverty. The first phase began in 2018, focusing on assisting low-income households in replacing old lightings to reduce their electricity expenses. The goal is to improve the lighting efficiency in low-income households, thus enhancing their overall quality of life. During the 3 phases (2018-2021), a total of 226 households received assistance in replacing their lighting equipments. Additionally, these households benefited from annual subsidies provided by the Social Affairs Bureau to improve their access to energy resources.

En effet, la Ville de Douala dispose d'un Plan directeur d'urbanisme d'une validité de 15 ans et dont la mise en œuvre a été chiffrée à un peu plus de 1500 milliards de F CFA tandis que  le budget de la ville se situe en moyenne à 60 milliards par an. La ville a pris l'option d'améliorer sa connaissance des changements climatiques et de leurs aléas à l'échelle locale à travers la mise en place d'un observatoire. Long-term ecological impacts on forest ecosystems, including loss of biodiversity.Tourism Industry:    Wildfires can deter tourists from visiting regions prone to fire events.    Reduced visitor numbers, cancellations, and negative perceptions of safety.    Economic losses for businesses relying on tourism and related services.Health Sector:    Wildfire smoke poses significant health risks, especially for vulnerable individuals.    Increased respiratory problems, aggravated asthma, and other respiratory illnesses.    Stress-related mental health issues among affected populations.    Strain on healthcare systems, emergency services, and resources.Infrastructure and Utilities:    Damage to critical infrastructure, such as power lines, roads, and communication networks. response_answer: New Taipei City, with its vast territory and large population, shoulders significant responsibilities in addressing climate change issues. Since 2016, the concept of climate change adaptation has been integrated into the city's regional planning, taking into account the future urban development of New Taipei City. In November 2020, the city officially signed the Climate Emergency Declaration, presenting the "2030 Climate Vision," and planned to establish the Climate Change and Energy Strategy Implementation Committee, which later transformed into the New Taipei City Climate Change Response Steering Groups in 2023. The aim is to build the city's mitigation and adaptation capabilities. The Steering Groups were approved on January 10, 2021 and include the "Resilience Adaptation Team" task force, focused on strengthening adaptation capacity, enhancing resilience, and reducing vulnerability to minimize the impact of climate risks and promptly respond to disasters while improving self-recovery capabilities.The Resilience and Adaptation Group, under the supervision of the New Taipei City Department of Urban and Rural Development, aligns with the "National Climate Change Action Guidelines" and the "National Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan (Years 107-111)." The adaptation efforts are divided into eight domains: "Disasters," "Infrastructure for Livelihood," "Water Resources," "Land Use," "Coastal Areas," "Energy Supply and Industries," "Agricultural Production and Biodiversity," and "Health." Strategies for adaptation are developed for each domain, and regular reviews are conducted (see Annex 1).In addition to complying with central government regulations, the city government conducted a comprehensive assessment and survey of the entire city in 2016 and released the "New Taipei City Climate Change Adaption Plan." This report referenced the IPCC AR5, local disaster data, and first-hand investigation interviews to identify "Disasters" and "Health" as priority areas for the city. It also developed improvement plans as a reference for New Taipei City's current adaptation efforts.This project is based on the ICLEI Adaptation Plan, the "Adaptation Policy Framework" developed by UNDP, the "Adaptation Wizard" of UKCIP, the assessment framework for the development of central units in Taiwan, and the "Guidelines for Planning Local Climate Change Adaptation Plans(Updated Version)", and the results of climate change risk assessment and disaster potential data collected from central units in Taiwan or agencies in New Taipei City.We first explore the possible hazards of temperature, rainfall, sea level rise, and extreme events caused by climate change, and identify key issues. The expert consultation meeting and the inter-bureau platform meeting were held to take stock of the climate change risks faced by the city and to map out the future risks of climate change.1. Consideration of vulnerable groups: This report describes the exposure of each disaster to different groups (including vulnerable groups: outdoor workforce, elderly population, disadvantaged groups, etc.).2. Considering the risk of transformation: In order to reduce the resistance to promote the policy of adaptation, we intend to combine industry, government, academia, civil society organizations and the general public and implement two-way communication, so that science, industry and the government can have cross-disciplinary dialogues to build consensus and obtain public support to maximize the effectiveness of policy implementation. We think from the public's perspective and provide smarter, more humane services.3. Consideration of high emission scenarios: The adjustment base period for this report is the year 1980 to the year 1999. The target years are the year 2020 to the year 2039, Taking the IPCC AR6 report released in 2022 as an example, although the scale of the report is large, the suggested strategies may not necessarily meet the specific needs of our country. However, the IPCC AR6 report breaks down disciplinary boundaries and aggregates 130 risks into "Eight Major System Risks." It incorporates social and economic development into future emission scenarios, replacing Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP) with Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP).4. Risk Management Framework: Based on the results of the risk analysis in this report (including adaptation enhancement plans and risk reduction methods), the City has developed climate change adaptation plans, disaster prevention and relief plans, pathways and effectiveness assessments in various areas of the City, and has implemented a number of adaptation measures.

column_name: Action description and web link to further information^
response_answer: S’adapter efficacement aux effets des changements climatiques nécessite un engagement de toute la société. Les consultations menées pendant le processus  Plan National d'adaptation aux changements climatiques du Cameroun (PNACC) ont montré qu’une grande majorité des populations et des décideurs est encore ignorantes des questions des changements climatiques. C’est pourquoi l’information sur les changements climatiques est un axe stratégique de ce premier PNACC. Il favorisera l’accès à l’information aux populations (en particulier en milieu rural), aux élus et aux étudiants. Il s’agit donc, à l’aide de la stratégie nationale de communication sur l’adaptation aux changements climatiques (élaborée en octobre 2011 en préambule du processus PNACC), de vulgariser l’information sur les risques dus aux impacts des changements climatiques et de promouvoir les mesures d’adaptation nécessaire. Deuxièmement, les connaissances sur les changements climatiques des acteurs publics (par exemple, au niveau des collectivités territoriales décentralisées  CTD) et privés (par exemple, dans les banques) doivent être renforcées. Enfin, il faut également éduquer et former les enseignants et les étudiants aux changements climatiques. Il s’agit donc, avec l’aide de la stratégie élaborée dans le cadre du programme PACC, d’intégrer des modules de formation aux changements climatiques dans les systèmes éducatifs du Cameroun.

question_name: Report your jurisdiction's most significant examples of collaboration with government, business, and/or civil society on climate-related issues.
response_answer: In the past, climate change policies were usually implemented through the top-down approach, however, if there exists a knowledge gap between the city government and communities, it’s difficult to bring about desired effects. On the other hand, if communities don’t have the opportunity to engage in planning, the adaptation plan may not correspond to the needs of communities. The importance of community engagement in adaptation planning is comprehensively recognized internationally, therefore the concept of “Community Based Adaptation” has been advocated by many organizations in the world. When the adaptation plan was being developed in 2018, the city government also communicated with local organizations and communities, in an effort to practice Community Based Adaptation.Before interacting with communities, the city government had identified the priority adaptation sectors of Taoyuan, and selected the communities to practice Community Based Adaptation as demonstration for each priority sector. After visiting potential communities, we cooperated with two villages, Kuangshing Village in Pingzhen District and Sihai Village in Dayuan District, to build adaptation infrastructure tailored to the needs of each village.The infrastructure includes underground rain water harvesting systems, permeable pavement, educational plates, etc. Besides, we also installed hydroelectric power to harness the water resources in Sihai Village. Apart from infrastructure, capacity building was also one of the main tasks. Given that Community Colleges are one of the important nodes for knowledge dissemination and mobilization in local networks, the city government also held a capacity building workshop in 2018. In the workshop, community workers learned the methodology of Community Based Adaptation, which is conducive to developing adaption projects and planning adaptation class in Community Colleges.(The attached file is the same as the one in question 1.1a. Although the name of the report includes ”Air Pollution”, the report is completely focused on climate risk and vulnerability assessment. The evidence of Community Based Adaptation is documented in chapter 4.5.)
