response_answer: Kaohsiung City is actively developing a diversified water supply. In 2013, the city government began to promote the recycling and reuse plan of discharged water. The source of reclaimed water obtained from sewage regeneration is not affected by the weather, so that a drop of water can be used at least twice, maximizing the use of water resources. To ensure industrial water use and reduce the pressure of water source scheduling during dry periods, The construction of Fengshan waste water treatment plant has been completed in 2019, which supply reclaimed water 45,000 tons/day.The reclaimed water project of Linhai waste water treatment Plant was completed in 2022. Afterwards, the city will supply a total of 78,000 tons/day of industrial water to the Linhai Industrial Zone, and the entire period can reach 100,000 tons/day, In the whole period, it can reach 110,000 tons/day, greatly reducing industrial water pressure. In addition, the North Kaohsiung reclaimed water project will also continue to be promoted, and the Qiaotou and Nanzi reclaimed water projects will be promoted. The Qiaotou reclaimed water is expected to supply 30,000 tons/day in 2026, and the Nanzi reclaimed water is expected to supply 70,000 tons/day  in 2028. In addition, there are prep groundwater supplying 130,000 tons/day, and the new addition is expected to supply 100,000 tons/day underflow water in 2026. It is believed that multi water resource management in Kaohsiung can also decrease the vulnerability and impacts of more frequent droughts.

response_answer: The actions include the following plans:1. Promoting the daily 30-kilometer happiness mileage      Launch the traffic policy "Happiness Mileage 30km" by the city government, for the purpose of encouraging citizens to take public transportation, so as to create a friendlier space for pedestrians and cyclists. Collectively enjoy 30-km “free” transportation mileages per day, in the future, for everyone using a "Citizen Card" to ride on Taoyuan public transportation (including Taoyuan buses and Youbike).2. Promoting the $1200-monthly commuting pass (called “TPASS”) in the living circle of Keelung City/ Taipei City/ New Taipei City/ Taoyuan City, and Taoyuan City/ Hsin-Chu County/ Hsin-Chu City/ Miaoli County, respectivelyMake the four cities, namely Keelung City/ Taipei City/ New Taipei City/ Taoyuan City, a common living circle, and create further benefits out of the past investments in public transportation by the four cities, by promoting the $1200-monthly TPASS in Keelung City/ Taipei City/ New Taipei City/ Taoyuan City.Allow the convenience, with one card in hand, of riding on public transportation such as urban buses, MRTs, TRA’s railways, passenger transportation via national highway, passenger transportation via highway, and public YouBikes in the living circle of Keelung City/ Taipei City/ New Taipei City/ Taoyuan City, thus reducing commuting costs between cities. Dynamically adjust extra trips of trains, by the cities’ Department of Transportation and the cities’ metro corporation, in response to the possible increase of passengers.The cost for a TPASS (in the living circle of Keelung City/ Taipei City/ New Taipei City/ Taoyuan City) is NT$1,200 per 30 days, which is about 60% off the actual monthly commuting cost. In the initial stage, Easy Cards can be used as a TPASS card. In phase II, iPASS among other cards can also be used as a TPASS card. TPASS can be used by anyone without restrictions (except that an Elder’s Card cannot be loaded with credits for TPASS), which can be used for unlimited rides within 30 days upon the activation of the card.Transportation vehicles applicable to a TPASS include all urban buses, MRTs, and public YouBikes in the living circle of Keelung City/ Taipei City/ New Taipei City/ Taoyuan City (excluding Happy Buses), provided the departure and destination points of a ride on the public transportation both fall within the highways, national highways, TRA’s railways, etc. in the living circle.The launch of TPASS is estimated to boost the users of TPASS to about 796,000 on a monthly basis. Three years after the launch of TPASS, the public transportation capacity of the four cities is expected to grow by 5% in comparison with year 2022, the traffic volume of private motor vehicles is expected to decrease by 5% in comparison with year 2022, and the accident rate or death rate per 100,000 motor vehicles is expected to decrease by 5%

question_name: Report your jurisdiction's most significant examples of collaboration with government, business, and/or civil society on climate-related issues.
response_answer: 1. According to the analysis of New Taipei City’s 2020 greenhouse gas inventory data, greenhouse gas emissions from the construction sector account for about 40% of the city’s total greenhouse gas emissions. New Taipei City launched the “New Taipei Energy-Saving E-House Project” in 2022. The E in “E-House Project” stands for “energy efficiency” – to put an emphasis on good houses that focus on energy efficiency, where the source efficiency is marked by a grading scale. By partnering with real estate agents, communities with excellent energy savings are posted on the real estate agent’s home sales website so the public can learn about the performance of the buildings in the community when purchasing or renting a home.2. The “New Taipei Energy-Saving E-House Project” converts the energy consumption of public utilities from the energy consumption density of public utilities (EUI for short), with smaller public utility EUI values meaning that the utility consumes less energy. The EUI value is graded according to the size of the metric, from three stars to six stars, with a higher star rating signifying higher energy efficiency. This will strengthen community residents’ sense of pride, affirm low-carbon and energy-saving actions, and drive nearby communities with energy-saving potential into joining the “New Taipei Energy Saving E-House,” creating a community atmosphere of autonomous energy saving.3. The “New Taipei Energy Saving E-House Project” enables people better to understand the energy consumption of their own public utilities. In the purchase of a home, the choice is also broader, just like with the beginning of the “energy efficiency label” for home appliances, more people are willing to buy products with higher energy efficiency, in addition to the sprouting of the concept of environmental protection in the minds of the public and, in the long run, they can save more money from electricity bills for their own wallets.4. In addition, the New Taipei City Government also provides related power-saving consultation and counseling, such as inviting experts to form a “power saving clinic” to make diagnoses and being counseled by a “low carbon community planner” with resources such as “low carbon community transformation” to help communities identify power consumption monsters. Through low-carbon retrofitting of public facilities, the city will reduce the electricity consumption of public facilities and gradually transform private sector buildings into “near-zero-carbon buildings,” gradually transforming New Taipei City into a zero-carbon city through the cooperation of enterprises, citizens and government to build a net-zero carbon community.

column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: Heat stress has significant impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors. The elderly are particularly susceptible to heat stress due to reduced ability to regulate body temperature, putting them at risk of heat-related illnesses and heatstroke. Children, especially infants and young children, are also vulnerable due to their smaller body mass and higher metabolic rates, making them prone to heat-related illnesses and dehydration. Individuals with chronic illnesses face exacerbated symptoms and health complications during heatwaves, with heat stress straining their cardiovascular and respiratory systems. Low-income groups may struggle to access cooling facilities or maintain adequate cooling in their homes, increasing their vulnerability to heat-related health issues. Outdoor workers in industries like construction and agriculture face a higher risk of heat-related illnesses due to prolonged exposure to high temperatures and physical exertion.Heat stress also impacts various sectors. In agriculture, high temperatures and water scarcity can lead to reduced crop yields, wilted plants, and livestock dehydration, affecting food security, agricultural livelihoods, and regional economies. The tourism and hospitality sectors can be affected as extreme heat deters tourists, impacts outdoor activities, and reduces visitor numbers, leading to economic losses. Energy and utilities infrastructure, especially electricity grids, can be strained during heatwaves due to increased demand for cooling systems, potentially causing power outages and disrupting essential services. The public health sector experiences an increased burden from heat-related illnesses, including heat exhaustion, heatstroke, respiratory problems, cardiovascular issues, and exacerbation of existing health conditions.

question_name: Provide details on your climate risk and vulnerability assessment.
response_answer: In this report, flood and heat wave adaptation measures were analyzed for the city of Can Tho (in selected districts) with respect to their cost-efficiency and effectiveness on adaptation and risk reduction. 17 measures (10 measures for flood, 4 measures for heat waves and 3 measures for both, flood and heat waves) were successfully assessed using the modelling platform CLIMADA. The Economics of Climate Adaptation (ECA) framework is set out to develop practical recommendations that enable national and local decision-makers to build a comprehensive assessment of the climate risk that their economies are facing while minimizing the cost of adaptation through cost-efficient strategies. A particular emphasis is made on a robust and integrated approach based on sound scientific facts. The ECA as applied here contains three elements supported by the modelling platform CLIMADA: 1. Climate risk identification: Conduct an identification of climate risk in a defined region (e.g. urban area), identify areas and people at risk, spanning all significant climate hazards and the full range of possible impacts for different sectors 2. Climate risk quantification: Calculate the expected damage across multiple climates and economic scenarios 3. Identification and prioritization of CCA measures (using Cost-Benefit Analysis of CCA measures): Determine strategies including a portfolio of specific CCA measures with detailed cost/benefit assessment. Additionally, ECA includes a strong component of stakeholder engagement to complement the hazard modelling and asset valuation. This report presents a brief overview of ECA and the main results of flood impact today and in the future using CLIMADA, a probabilistic modelling platform.

column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: Infectious diseases in Delhi, exacerbated by factors like urbanization and climate change, disproportionately impact various vulnerable groups, magnifying existing inequalities and posing distinct challenges. The Covid-19 pandemic highlighted the effect of the virus on the vulnerable populations. Women and girls often face increased caregiving responsibilities, limited healthcare access, and disrupted education during outbreaks. Low-income populations, residing in densely populated and resource-constrained areas, encounter higher transmission risks due to inadequate sanitation and healthcare facilities. The elderly, with weakened immune systems and co-morbidities, are at greater risk of severe outcomes. Children and youth, especially in overcrowded living conditions, are susceptible to infections, while school closures disrupt education and hinder proper development. These challenges amplify existing inequalities, necessitating urgent interventions. Comprehensive public health measures, improved healthcare access, sanitation infrastructure, and community-based strategies are essential to mitigate the disproportionate impact of infectious diseases on these vulnerable groups and ensure a more equitable and resilient health landscape in Delhi. In the past month, there has been a rise in cases of malaria for the city of Delhi as a result of climate change. Infectious diseases in Delhi have wide-ranging impacts across sectors. The healthcare system faces strain from increased patient load, while economic productivity declines due to worker absenteeism and healthcare costs. Education is disrupted by school closures, and tourism, hospitality, agriculture, and transportation sectors suffer due to reduced activity. Trade, commerce, social services, real estate, entertainment, and events are also adversely affected. Effective public health strategies and cross-sector coordination are vital to mitigate the far-reaching consequences of infectious diseases on society and the economy.

question_name: Provide information on your jurisdiction’s oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities and how these issues have impacted your jurisdiction's planning.
column_name: Describe how climate-related issues have impacted your jurisdiction's master/development planning
response_answer: Climate-related concerns have significantly influenced Delhi's master and development planning, resulting in a concerted effort to integrate climate resilience and sustainability into various aspects of urban growth. The city's response encompasses strategies to mitigate urban heat islands and heatwaves through green spaces and cool infrastructure, address air quality and emissions through cleaner transportation and industry norms, manage water scarcity and flooding with sustainable water systems, enhance infrastructure resilience to extreme weather events, promote biodiversity and green spaces, encourage sustainable transport options, improve waste management practices, and strengthen disaster preparedness. This comprehensive approach reflects Delhi's commitment to creating a climate-resilient and sustainable urban environment that prioritizes the well-being of its residents while addressing the challenges posed by a changing climate.1. The first four key areas of the Delhi Master Plan 2041 are environment, water, critical resources and mobility. Out of the three goals mentioned in Vision 2042, the first is "Become an environmentally sustainable city that provides a healthy environment for its citizens and is adaptable towards addressing impacts of climate change".2. Promoting clean economic activities- Polluting industries as per list given at Annexure 1 shall not be permitted tooperate within Delhi. The list shall be updated by GNCTD and DDA periodically, based on directives of concerned authorities.3. Minimizing vehicular pollution - a. Adoption of mix-use and TOD for reducing the average trip lengths and bringing jobs and homes closer to transit networks.b. Improving public transport infrastructure - The DMRC is currently engaged in the construction of Phase 4. The 65.2 km stretch covers three priority corridors spanning 45 stations — Janakpuri West-RK Ashram Marg (28.92 km), Majlis Park-Maujpur (12.55 km),  Tughalakabad-Aerocity (23.62 km);  a fleet of 150 electric buses have also been added,  the government plans to add 1500 electric buses, the approval for the same in underway (https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/delhi/delhi-govt-to-give-final-nod-to-procure-1500-e-buses-in-two-weeks-7944959/)c. Migration to green fuels for public transport as well as IPT and other shared modes through appropriate incentives.4. The following mitigation measures shall be adopted across the city, and implemented on a priority basis within identified pollution, flooding or heating hotspots in the city:a. Pavements, roads and roofs shall be constructed/coated with light coloured material with high albedo value wherever possible. This can reduce local temperature by 3-5 degrees.b. Road sections shall include appropriate trees and buffers to reduce air and noise pollution. Sustainable urban drainage components such as bioswales, rain gardens, etc., shall also be incorporated (including in residual areas below flyovers) to mitigate water logging.c. Native species of trees and plants which act as pollution filters shall be included in the various greening initiatives. Miyawaki forests, smog absorption towers and other technological solutions may also be adopted for mitigating pollution at hotspots.d. Higher Green Blue Factor (GBF) values i.e. higher greening requirements may be prescribed for future developments in areas identified as chronic pollution hotspots. Similarly, ground coverage may be restricted and pervious surface requirements may be increased in areas identified as flooding hotspots in the city.e. All new developments shall locate facilities like hospitals, schools, old age homes etc., away from high-speed traffic corridors.f. A Noise Pollution Action Plan may be prepared and implemented by GNCTD based on the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules (2000) or any  other government recommended guidance framework. The number and  spread of noise pollution monitoring stations in the city to be increased and  appropriate noise reduction measures (plantation or noise barriers) may be implemented for immediate relief in noise hotspots.

response_answer: In 2021, the "New Taipei Safe Business Epidemic Prevention and Energy-Saving Measures Subsidy" program was launched to provide subsidies to local businesses and service providers for installing PVC door curtains and ceiling fans. PVC door curtains can separate indoor and outdoor spaces or front and back counter areas, effectively preventing droplet transmission and air conditioning leakage. Ceiling fans promote indoor air circulation and energy efficiency, saving 18% of air conditioning energy consumption. question_name: Report your jurisdiction's most significant examples of collaboration with government, business, and/or civil society on climate-related issues.
response_answer: The changes in people's living habits and economic environment in recent years have led to an increase in the quantity and variety of surplus materials year after year. In order to reuse resources and reduce waste of resources, an action strategy based on the public market, the principle of cross-agency integration, and private and public cooperation hereby have been adopted so that surplus resources can be effectively distributed to the disadvantaged. Since the year 2016, a food sharing network, which is implemented as follows, has been established.1. Constructing a public welfare-oriented resource supply and demand networkThrough cross-departmental cooperation, the city government has integrated the concept of food conservation into its existing policies to promote and publicize the concept of food conservation at the industry and educational levels.In cooperation with fruit and vegetable distribution companies, public markets, food enterprises, and community outlets, we have been building a supply and demand network for extra products and offcuts, which will be used for community meals for the disadvantaged to reduce food waste along the production chain in the city.2. Private and Public CollaborationIn order to ensure the food safety of the clients served by the common dining base and  to prevent the surplus materials from deteriorating during the transportation process, which results in double wastage, the private and public sector cooperated with civil welfare organizations to match three refrigerated (frozen) trucks to assist in the distribution of ingredients in remote areas. In addition to reducing the inequality between urban and rural areas in terms of access to resources, it also allows the donor companies to have more trust in the city in terms of preserving and transporting the ingredients and consolidating the cooperative relationship. Starting from year 2020,  in order to improve the preservation of ingredients and the convenience of using them in community units, the ingredients donated by enterprises have been made into frozen seasoning kits through social welfare organizations to improve the preservation period and the efficiency of using them.

question_name: Identify and describe the most significant factors impacting on your jurisdiction’s ability to adapt to climate change and indicate how those factors either support or challenge this ability.
column_name: Describe how the factor supports or challenges the adaptive capacity of your jurisdiction^
response_answer: Some challenging factors are shown below:- Aging infrastructure: Aging infrastructure can be more vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Deteriorating roads, bridges, drainage systems, and buildings may not be able to withstand extreme weather events such as floods, storms, or intense rainfall, impeding the city's ability to adapt effectively.- Inadequate infrastructure design: Infrastructure that has been designed without considering climate change projections and future risks may be ill-equipped to handle the changing climate. Insufficient flood control measures, inadequate drainage systems, and improper building design can increase the vulnerability of infrastructure to climate-related hazards.- Lack of maintenance and repair: Inadequate maintenance and repair of existing infrastructure can compromise its functionality and resilience. Failure to address issues such as clogged drains, damaged levees, or deteriorating buildings can exacerbate the impacts of climate change, hinder adaptation efforts, and increase the costs of future repairs.- Insufficient infrastructure capacity: Inadequate infrastructure capacity to handle increased demand due to population growth, urbanization, and climate change can strain the city's ability to adapt. Insufficient water supply, limited transportation systems, and inadequate waste management infrastructure can hinder resilience-building efforts and limit the city's adaptive capacity.

response_answer: The emissions breakdown by sector reveals that the industrial sector accounted for 83%, the residential and commercial sector accounted for 9.1%, the transportation sector accounted for 7%, the environmental and agricultural sector accounted for 0.8%. In the industrial sector, the formation of the Net-Zero Industry Alliance allows for collaboration and guidance from experts in greenhouse gas inventory, energy-saving and carbon reduction. By identifying emission sources and implementing reduction measures, the aim is to minimize the climate-related costs associated with international CBAM or domestic carbon fees.In the residential and commercial sectors, efforts are made to promote energy efficiency disclosure and improvement in both public and private buildings. The government provides subsidies for energy-efficient appliances to support the active participation of vulnerable groups in energy-saving and carbon reduction initiatives.In the  transport sector, due to its special geographical characteristics, the population distribution in Kaohsiung is uneven. 95% of the population lives in the metropolitan area that only accounts for 25% of the city’s overall area. Therefore, it depends on the comprehensive public transportation networks that integrated the MRT, Kaohsiung Light Rail, buses, sharing E-scooters and bikes, Taxi+Bus, and YouBike 2.0 to provide convenient and safe transportation to residents. In the aspect of transportation equity, the city government is committed to reducing the gap between public transportation in urban and rural areas.

response_answer: The impact of land use planning on the city's ability to adapt to climate change can support its adaptation efforts as follows:- Climate-resilient infrastructure: Land use planning allows for the integration of climate resilience into infrastructure development. This includes designing and locating buildings, transportation systems, and utilities in a way that minimizes exposure to climate hazards and promotes adaptive design principles. Climate-resilient infrastructure can withstand extreme weather events and reduce vulnerabilities.- Green and blue infrastructure: Incorporating green spaces, urban forests, wetlands, and other natural features into land use planning promotes ecosystem services, such as flood control, heat mitigation, and biodiversity conservation. Green and blue infrastructure supports climate change adaptation by enhancing urban resilience, reducing urban heat island effects, and improving water management.- Mixed-use and compact development: Land use planning that promotes mixed-use and compact development reduces urban sprawl, decreases transportation emissions, and improves access to services and amenities. This compact and connected development pattern supports sustainable and climate-friendly lifestyles, reducing the carbon footprint and promoting climate change adaptation.

column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: Regarding the phenomena and trends of climate change, as assessed in IPCC AR6, it is projected that with further warming, each region will experience an increasing number of events driven by multiple climate influences. Compound heatwaves, heavy rainfall, and droughts are expected to become more frequent. The probability of extreme sea-level events that historically occurred once in a century is increasing. Tropical cyclones or extratropical storms may intensify, and droughts and wildfires are likely to increase.New Taipei City is located in a subtropical region, adjacent to the coast. Based on the downscaled information from the Taiwan Climate Change Projection and Information Platform (TCCIP) using AR6 data, it is estimated that future disasters that pose the greatest risks to vulnerable populations in the city include heatwaves and damage to infrastructure caused by storms. High temperatures will lead to an increase in heat-related illnesses, including heatstroke, and the probability of related deaths and illnesses, particularly among the elderly. Storms will cause damage to critical urban infrastructure such as buildings, transportation networks, power plants, and crops, posing the highest risk to residents in coastal areas.

response_answer: Within Kaohsiung City, there are three Taiwan Power Company(Taipower) thermal power plants: Hsinta, Dalin, and Nanpu. These plants have a total installed capacity of 6,878 MW. In addition, Kaohsiung City, as an industrial city, has 17 cogeneration plants and 35 boilers, primarily fueled with coal and natural gas, with a total installed capacity of 1,275 MW. It plays a vital role in Taiwan's energy supply. To reduce GHG emissions from energy generation, efforts are made to gradually increase the proportion of natural gas in power generation. Furthermore, the evaluation and gradual adoption of low-carbon fuels such as hydrogen and solid recovered fuel (SRF) are being considered. To accelerate the energy transition, Kaohsiung City established the "Green Energy Promotion Task Force" at the municipal level in 2020. Vice Mayor Charles Lin has served as the convener, with the support of the Economic Development Bureau and Public Works Bureau. Various city government departments, including the Environmental Protection Bureau, Water Resources Bureau, Education Bureau, Civil Affairs Bureau, Police Department, Agriculture Bureau, Marine Bureau, and Urban Development Bureau, were working together to further promote the goals. The task force has set a target of 1.25GW of renewable energy capacity from 2021 to 2026, focusing on three aspects: "energy-creating," "energy-saving," and "energy-storing." Due to sufficient sunlight, Kaohsiung City actively develops solar energy and has reached an installed capacity of 950 MW as of March 2023, ranking fifth in Taiwan. The city also continues to develop biogas power generation from landfill and livestock waste.As industrial emissions account for more than 80% of the total emissions in Kaohsiung City, a "Net-Zero Industry Alliance" has been established with companies with major emission sources. Through industry leaders leading the way and state-owned enterprises setting an example, the alliance aims to share carbon reduction technologies, promote cross-industry collaboration, and require industries to set short, medium, and long-term reduction goals and plans to achieve carbon reduction.

response_answer: At the end of 2020, Can Tho has 1,036 poor households with 3,090 people and more than 9,000 near-poor households with 34,729 people. The poor are particularly vulnerable to natural disasters and changing economic situations. Living by canals in poorly built houses, the poor are significantly at risk from floods, typhoons, and other extreme weather events. Furthermore, the elderly, children, the disabled and other vulnerable groups are even more at risk due to limited access to public services.In early 2021, the city government requested relevant departments, agencies, and mass organizations to synchronously implement policies and projects to support the poor in health, education, housing, and preferential credit, incentives, agricultural extension, vocational training, job creation, etc. The city required a provision of free health insurance for the poor and full implementation of educational support policies for poor students.

question_name: Report on how climate change impacts health outcomes and health services in your jurisdiction.
response_answer: Due to the impact of global warming, Taiwan has experienced not only an increase in average temperatures in recent years but also an increase in the number of hot days throughout the year. In response to this, the New Taipei City Government has developed the "New Taipei City Government Heatwave Response Implementation Plan" and the "New Taipei City Government Cold Wave Preparedness Measures Implementation Plan" to ensure proper care and minimize harm to vulnerable groups such as homeless individuals and elderly people living alone during extreme heatwaves and cold waves.Groups vulnerable to high temperatures span regions, races, and ages. Young children, the elderly, outdoor workers (e.g., farmers, land builders, and motorcycle couriers), low-income households, travellers, the sick, people receiving medication that affects body temperature regulation, and institutional residents (e.g., nursing homes and social welfare agencies) are all at high risk. In addition, the humidity will aggravate the impact, and the impact will be greater in urban areas of New Taipei City than in rural areas because of the heat island effect.

response_answer: The urban growth in Antalya in recent years with the increasing population has led to the expansion of artificial areas in the city. The risk of flooding and flooding increases as rainwater cannot reach the ground. In this respect, first of all, the ground of certain places in risky areas in the city should be covered with a water-permeable surface. Then, the use of water-permeable surfaces should be expanded throughout the city. Especially covering the hard floors in areas closed to traffic, sidewalks, bicycle paths and parks with this material is one of the solutions that will minimize the risk of flooding and flooding in these areas in a possible rainfall.

question_name: Report on how climate change impacts health outcomes and health services in your jurisdiction.
response_answer: Antalya is one of the provinces with the highest number of storms and tornadoes in Turkey, but it is also affected by high temperatures, especially in summer. Therefore, it is essential to take precautions knowing that the effects of climate change will create more risks in certain areas and population groups. It is clear that there has not been a detailed study on the direct effects of climate change on public health in the city, but there is a need for such a detailed study on extreme weather events.  In the report prepared by AFAD in 2021, the number of vulnerable population groups was determined based on data from the Provincial Directorate of Family and Social Services.  The ratio of the number of people with severe disabilities and in need of care in Antalya was calculated as 0.92. Although this rate remains low compared to the population, the number of vulnerable population in Kepez, Muratpaşa, Alanya and Manavgat districts varies between 1000 and 4000. Although climate change will affect the entire city, its impact on the vulnerable population will be much more devastating. For this reason, the development of climate change adaptation strategies should first be developed for the areas where these populations live predominantly and then should be generalized throughout the city. Antalya is a city that encounters climatic disasters quite frequently. Both its geographical structure and climate structure cause the city to have many and varied weather events. In addition to these, the fact that the climatic situation is changing day by day and the earth's temperature is increasing leads to the frequency and intensity of climatic disasters. In Antalya, floods, landslides, rockfalls, avalanches and heavy snowfall, earthquakes, fires, storms and tornadoes, heat waves and frost are observed.  Due to the fact that Antalya is the 5th largest province of the country and the risks it faces, Antalya Provincial Disaster and Emergency Directorate (Antalya AFAD) was established with the law in 2009.

response_answer: As risky as tornadoes, storms and excessive rainfall are for Antalya, the destruction caused by heat waves and the urban heat island effect is just as risky. Heat waves, which will directly affect the health of people living in urban areas, are even more effective due to buildings, roads and other gray infrastructure systems. For this reason, it is very important for Antalya to identify areas with urban heat island effect and to transform these areas into ecosystem services with natural-based solutions. Considering the urbanization rate and population density, it is possible to talk about the large number of areas where the urban heat island effect is intense throughout the city of Antalya. Therefore, it is clear that risk and vulnerability maps should be made by expert teams in order to reduce and prevent the impact.

column_name: Describe how climate-related issues have impacted your jurisdiction's master/development planning
response_answer: As we all know, global climate change is a situation that should be recognized as affecting the whole world. Our country, which is located in the Mediterranean Basin, will be exposed to many effects from this situation, especially drought, floods and an increase in extreme weather events. The fact that Antalya, the city we live in, has a livable, healthy and sustainable environment and economy reveals that this issue should be taken into consideration in the coming period. The issue of adaptation to climate change is gaining importance in order to take appropriate measures to prevent or minimize the damage that may be caused by predicting the negative effects of climate change and to take advantage of the opportunities that may arise. We are determinedly continuing our efforts to make Antalya, the capital of agriculture and tourism and the 5th largest city with a population of approximately 2.6 million, an environment and nature-friendly city. As Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, we continue to carry out not short-term, day-saving projects, but planned, rule-based, technique and science-based continuous environmental projects that take into account the rights of future generations, with a city vision and common sense. With the projects and practices we carry out on behalf of all the people of Antalya, the 18 environmental awards we have received at local, national and international level during our term in office are proof of our sensitivity to the environment.Local policies are as important as national policies in mitigating the negative effects of climate change. In this context, the Western Mediterranean Development Agency (BAKA) TR61 Level 2 Regional Plan (2014- 2023) covering the provinces of Antalya Isparta Burdur and Antalya Metropolitan Municipality (2020-2024) Strategic Plan are examined as local policies that can contribute to the action plan for Antalya province.According to BAKA TR61 Level 2 Regional Plan (2014-2023), in the Regional Spatial Development Diagram, which shows the activities targeted to be carried out during the plan period, the western transportation corridor connecting the Antalya metropolitan area with the inner part of the region shows the development of the region's industry. The number of foreign tourists visiting Antalya, also known as the city of tourism, increased by more than 100% between 2003 and 2012 and rose to third place in the ranking of the most visited cities in the world. While it is known that climate change affects many sectors, Antalya province is also affected. In this context, it is important to avoid practices and actions that increase the effects of climate change. The Regional Plan also aims to ensure the integration of transportation routes for the province of Antalya and to implement multimodal transportation, while maritime transportation is also aimed to be developed.In the 2020-2024 Strategic Plan of Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, the ninth strategic objective is defined as "To ensure the formation of a planned, modern, aesthetic and livable city by guiding the social and economic development of the city in accordance with its natural, historical and cultural texture" and Target 9.5 is stated as "To plan and realize activities against disasters and earthquakes that may occur throughout the city". The tenth strategic objective in the Strategic Plan is "to create a green and healthy city that respects nature", and Target 10.1 "To maintain and increase the amount of green areas", Target 10.2 "To protect the environment and human health, to create a city with a high quality of life and to activate and disseminate social awareness in this field", Target 10.3 "To increase social awareness for a clean and healthy city, to activate waste management" and Target 10.4 "To carry out the necessary analyzes and inspections related to public health and to improve them in line with accreditation processes". Target 11.6 "To develop and diversify renewable energy resources" is included under the "To plan infrastructure works to increase the quality of urban life", which is stated as another strategic objective. Strategic Objective 12 "To plan and develop agricultural infrastructure services, to increase agricultural production, to make rural living areas livable and aesthetic with their infrastructure and superstructure" is supported by Target 12.2 "To protect, plan, improve agricultural resources and increase producer awareness". In Strategic Goal 13, eighteen targets have been set for transportation under the heading "to provide planned, rational, high quality, safe and integrated public transportation services with the rail system, taking into account the future population density of the city".

question_name: Provide details of your emissions reduction target(s). Please report both long-term and mid-term targets, if applicable.
response_answer: The New Taipei City government has set its legally binding emission reduction target for 2030, taking into account both the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and the results planned by the central government of our country. However, the New Taipei City Climate Change Response Steering Groups will continue to strive for the SBTi as its ambitious goal.Based on the SBTi and WWF-OPCC methodology, Taiwan's HDI (Human Development Index) in 2018 was 0.911. It is estimated that New Taipei City's emission reduction target for 2030 (using 2005 as the base year) is 62%.According to Article 3 of the Electricity Act in Taiwan, the "analysis, formulation, and promotion of electricity policies" are under the authority of the central government. The power supply in Taiwan is planned and managed by the Taiwan Power Company, which is granted by the central government. The company operates power plants throughout the country and allocates power to various counties and cities.Examining the emission structure of New Taipei City, the emissions from Scope 1 accounted for 36.12% in 2020, while the emissions from Scope 2 accounted for 63.87%. The emissions from Scope 2 are mainly influenced by the carbon intensity of electricity determined by the central government. Additionally, the setting of energy efficiency standards in the industrial sector falls under the responsibility of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. Therefore, the emission reduction target of New Taipei City must consider the decarbonization progress of electricity by the central government and align with the overall national reduction plan. The current plan by the central government in Taiwan is to reduce the carbon intensity of electricity to 0.424 kgCO2e/kWh by 2025 (compared to 0.559 kgCO2e/kWh in 2005). The overall emission reduction target set by the central government is to reduce the total emissions by 24% ± 1% by 2030 (using 2005 as the base year).Considering both SBTi and domestic regulations, New Taipei City has set a 30% emission reduction target for 2030 (using 2005 as the base year). However, the city actively cooperates with the central government to accelerate the construction of renewable energy facilities. For example, it joined the "The Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) " in 2019 to support the phase-out of coal-fired boilers in the industrial sector within its jurisdiction. The "Sulfur-Ziping Geothermal Power Demonstration Zone" will be completed by 2025, and by 2030, an inventory will be conducted to identify the potential for renewable energy installation in public and private sectors, as well as public buildings, with a target of achieving 150 MW of renewable energy capacity. Since energy resources in Taiwan are centrally distributed nationwide, the effectiveness of these policies is shared across the country and does not solely reflect the emission reduction efforts of the energy sector in New Taipei City.

column_name: Describe the risks to your jurisdiction related to the transition to a low-carbon economy
response_answer: The transition to a low-carbon economy in Can Tho City presents both opportunities and risks. While the transition is essential for mitigating climate change and reducing GHG emissions, it can also pose challenges and risks to the city. Here are some potential risks associated with the transition to a low-carbon economy in Can Tho City:Economic impacts: Can Tho City's economy is currently dependent on sectors that contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, such as agriculture, manufacturing, and energy-intensive industries. A rapid transition to a low-carbon economy may result in disruptions to these sectors and the potential loss of jobs. It is crucial to manage this transition carefully, ensuring that alternative economic opportunities are created and affected workers are supported through retraining programs and social safety nets.Technological and infrastructure challenges: The transition to a low-carbon economy often requires the adoption of new technologies and infrastructure. This can pose challenges in terms of technology availability, affordability, and implementation. Can Tho City will need to invest in research and development, capacity building, and infrastructure upgrades to support the deployment of renewable energy systems, energy-efficient buildings, and sustainable transportation networks.Financial implications: The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial investments in renewable energy projects, energy efficiency measures, and sustainable infrastructure. Can Tho City may face challenges in accessing the necessary financing for these initiatives, especially if there is limited access to international climate finance or insufficient domestic financial resources. It is important to develop innovative financial mechanisms, attract private sector investments, and explore partnerships to overcome these challenges.Social equity and affordability: The costs associated with the transition to a low-carbon economy, such as higher energy prices or changes in employment patterns, can impact vulnerable communities disproportionately. Ensuring social equity and affordability during the transition is crucial to avoid exacerbating existing inequalities. Can Tho City should prioritize policies and measures that consider the needs of low-income households, provide support for vulnerable groups, and ensure affordable access to clean energy and sustainable services.Adaptation and resilience: While transitioning to a low-carbon economy is crucial for mitigating climate change, Can Tho City also needs to address the risks posed by climate impacts. These risks include sea-level rise, increased frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, and changes in rainfall patterns. It is important to integrate climate adaptation and resilience measures into the transition planning process, considering factors such as coastal protection, water management, and urban planning to minimize the vulnerability of the city to future climate risks.

response_answer: The goal of "Baogao Smart Industrial Park" is to introduce production processes that meet the requirements of "low and zero pollution", with the main focus on smart city industries such as digital health, AI, information and communication and cloud computing, and low-polluting manufacturing. Electric vehicle industries such as Hon Hai and Tesla have entered this area.The first phase of Baogao Park has an investment of NT$4.1 billion and is already completed in 2022. The buildings in the park have obtained the "Gold-level Green Building Label" and "Silver-level Smart Building Label", and integrates "production", "life" and "ecology" concepts. In addition to integrating in the park the R&D, design, experiment and manufacturing required by the smart city industry to provide a flexible and mutually beneficial industrial space, it also has a 5G environment and various life functions, shaping the new “three-in-one” type of forward-looking area. The second phase is expected to be completed in 2026, with an estimated investment of NT$27 billion.In the future, Baogao Smart Industrial Park will become an important base for the promotion of green industries. In addition to public service facilities such as factory offices and conference halls, it will set up experimental fields, testing centers, youth innovation and incubation centers and R&D offices. The construction in the whole region aims at the gold level of green building, supplemented with the surrounding ecological restoration plan. It is estimated that the CO2 emission in the building's life cycle will be reduced by more than 20%, the annual energy consumption will be saved by more than 25%, the tap water consumption will be saved by 35%, and the resource recovery rate will reach 60%. Recycled materials will be introduced for the building materials and the Building Information Modeling (BIM) technology will be adopted to ensure overall environmental benefits throughout the entire life cycle.Links:1. It considers the need for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, enhancing energy efficiency, promoting renewable energy sources, improving waste management, and developing climate-resilient infrastructure.Furthermore, climate-related scenarios inform the prioritization of adaptation measures in the action plan. Can Tho City identifies sectors and areas that are most vulnerable to climate change and integrates adaptation strategies into its policies and projects. This may include measures such as flood control infrastructure, water resource management, sustainable agriculture practices, and urban planning that accounts for climate resilience.The action plan also recognizes the importance of capacity-building and technology transfer to effectively address climate change challenges. It may include provisions for training and equipping the workforce with the necessary knowledge and skills to implement green growth initiatives and leverage appropriate technologies for climate adaptation and mitigation.

column_name: Describe the impacts on vulnerable populations and sectors^
response_answer: Can Tho City generally faces a lower risk of wildfires compared to areas with dense forests or dry grasslands. The Mekong Delta is primarily characterized by wetland ecosystems, agricultural land, and a network of rivers and canals. However, it's important to consider the potential risk of wildfires in certain circumstances. Here are some factors to consider regarding the risk of wildfires in Can Tho City:1. Dry Season: During the dry season, which typically occurs from December to April, Can Tho City experiences lower rainfall and higher temperatures. Although the region is predominantly characterized by wetlands, the dry season can lead to drying of vegetation, such as grasses and agricultural residues. Under these conditions, the risk of accidental fires and the spread of wildfires can increase.2. Agricultural Practices: Can Tho City is known for its agricultural activities, including rice cultivation and aquaculture. Agricultural practices, such as the burning of crop residues or land clearing, can occasionally result in unintentional fires if not adequately managed. It's crucial to ensure responsible agricultural practices and proper disposal of agricultural waste to minimize the risk of wildfires.3. Human Activities: Human activities, such as unauthorized burning, campfires, or careless disposal of cigarettes, can potentially start fires. Accidental or intentional acts of negligence can contribute to the ignition and spread of wildfires, even in areas not typically prone to such events.4. Climate Change: Climate change can have indirect effects on the risk of wildfires. Rising temperatures, changes in precipitation patterns, and extended dry periods can create more favorable conditions for the occurrence and spread of fires. While the immediate risk may be relatively lower in wetland areas like Can Tho City, the broader regional and global climate changes can impact fire dynamics.

Based on Taiwan INDC emission reduction goal, Kaohsiung evaluate its future reduction goal and strengthen its efforts on emission reduction in each stage. Our emission reduction goal is to reduce 30% emission by 2030 and reached netzero emission in 2050. The “Greenhouse Gas Reduction and Management Act” will be revised and Kaohsiung City has already declared to follow Taiwan’s Pathway to Net-Zero Emissions in 2050. For the short-term GHG reduction target: a 30% reduction emission by 2030, compared to 2005 levels. We carry out effective mitigation and adaptation actions, such as replacing two-stroke scooters with electric scooters, green roof project, Kaohsiung House Project, solar PV project, green funeral services, electric car sharing system and so on.

response_answer: Kaohsiung Light Rail System is the first light rail system in Taiwan. The Light Rail, also known as Circular Line, interchange with both the Orange and Red MRT lines, which bisect the city and meet at Formosa Boulevard in the city center. With the launch of Kaohsiung's light rail loop and its planned integration with the Kaohsiung MRT, the effectiveness of Kaohsiung's public transportation system is expected to advance. In addition, light rail trains have low floors, providing a disabled-friendly riding environment that helps promote public use of mass transportation.Phase I construction consists of a section of line from Station C1 to Station C14, where Stations C3 and C14 are the transfer stations to Kaohsiung Mass Rapid Transit system's Red Line and Orange Line, respectively. The line begins at Lizihnei, following the harbour side and serving business districts, major shopping centers, education institutes, a stadium, the exhibition center, and museums before reaching Hamasen (locatoin). It expands the service demand for commuting, schooling, and tourism. Currently, the section of the Circular Light Rail from Museum Station (C20) to Love River Station (C24) is in operation, effectively connecting the "Taiwan Railways Museum Station" and "MRT Aozihdi Station." The completion of the route from Love River Station (C24) to Victory Park Station (C32) is expected by the end of 2023, achieving full-line operation.

The store is equipped with "i circle high-performance intelligent recycling machines" for recycling PET bottles and batteries. question_name: Report on your engagement with other levels of government regarding your jurisdiction's climate action.
response_answer: The city government utilized the methodology suggested by the Taiwan Climate Change Projection Information and Adaption Knowledge Platform (TCCIP) to predict climate changes and identify risk and vulnerability for Taoyuan in the future. On the other hand, In 2009, the Ministry of Science and Technology of Taiwan launched the Taiwan Integrated Research Program on Climate Change Adaptation Technology (TaiCCAT). Taoyuan used the assessment tool and the six-step cycle developed in TaiCCAT in 2018 to evaluate the weaknesses of Taoyuan City's historical climate change adaptation plan and improve it. Apart from using the methodology suggested by the national government, local governments also need resources and data at national level to develop adaptation strategies and implement initiatives. As a result, the city government also visited National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction (NCDR) in 2018 to apply for further data and discuss opportunities of cooperation in the future.(The attached file is the same as the one in question 1.1a. Although the name of the report includes ”Air Pollution”, the report is completely focused on climate risk and vulnerability assessment. The evidence of visiting the national government is documented in chapter 4.1.2.)

response_answer: In 2020, Kaohsiung City aligned its indicator structure with the United Nations’ and Taiwan’s sustainable development goals, and set 135 sustainability-related KPIs for 2020-2024. The main SDGs for Kaohsiung City include: no poverty, good health and well-being, clean water and sanitation, industry, innovation and infrastructure, sustainable cities and communities, responsible consumption and production, and climate action. Below are some examples of climate actions in different sectors such as transportation, residential, and industrial:1. Transportation: The MeNGO Card Monthly Pass service allows unlimited use of public transportation in Kaohsiung City, including MRT, buses, light rail, ferries, and the first 30 minutes of YouBike(shared bicycle) usage, all for NT$399. At the end of public transportation routes, taxis are used instead of buses as a scheduled and reservation-based service. In the past, residents in remote areas had to pay high fares of around NT$500-600 for services. By taking the bus-like taxis, they only need to pay the bus fare of NT$24 for two sections. Elderly and disabled passengers can ride for free by using their cards.https://men-go.tw/2. Residential: The Kaohsiung Lohas 4.0, also known as "KaoHouse," entered its fourth phase in 2022. The project focuses on improving air quality, increasing green space, providing accessiblities, and creating healthy homes. It aligns with the government's green building regulation, promotes rooftop greening to enhance urban green spaces, and supports the central government's efforts to rebuild dangerous and old buildings. The Kaohsiung Lohas 4.0 project allows exemptions from the payment of feedback fees for the construction of green energy facilities.https://build.kcg.gov.tw/index.aspx?au_id=41&sub_id=2443. Industrial: In response to international trends, the establishment of the "Net-Zero Industry Alliance" aims to promote the transformation with the big compaines as examples while guiding the small. A carbon inventory counseling group has been set up to improve upstream carbon footprint coefficients and provide carbon reduction and inventory counseling services to downstream businesses, in order to adapt to future trends.https://reurl.cc/eDn3mW

response_answer: The SBT (Science-Based Targets) calculation method chosen by Kaohsiung City is the C40 Deadline 2020 methodology. The calculation is as follows:1. Based on data provided by the Environmental Protection Bureau, the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting, and Statistics and the National Development Council, the following information is available:a. In 2015, the per capita greenhouse gas emissions in Kaohsiung City were 20.33 metric tons of CO2e. (source 1)b. The average per capita income in 2015 was NT$319,905 (equivalent to approximately US$10,488). (source 2)c. The estimated population of Kaohsiung City in 2030 is 2,711,242. (source 3)2. Comparing with the emission reduction ranges specified in the Deadline 2020 methodology, Kaohsiung City's emission reduction target for 2030 should be set at -10% to -15% based on the reference year(2015). Taking the highest reduction target of -15%, the estimated per capita greenhouse gas emissions for 2030 after reduction would be 17.28 metric tons. 3. Therefore, the emission reduction target for Kaohsiung City in 2030 (with the base year of 2005) is -27.40%. The target set by Kaohsiung City of a 30% reduction by 2030 exceeds the requirements of the C40 Deadline 2020 methodology.Sources:(1)Per capita greenhouse gas emissions: Please refer to the attached emissions inventory.(2)GDP: https://winsta.dgbas.gov.tw/DgbasWeb/ZWeb/StateFile_ZWeb.aspx(3)Estimated population of Kaohsiung City in 2030: National Population Projections( https://pop-proj.ndc.gov.tw/main_en/index.aspx )

Displacement and Homelessness: Floods can force people to evacuate their homes, leading to temporary or even long-term displacement and homelessness for affected communities.4. The assessment might have focused on other sectors with available data on fossil fuel consumption and electricity usage to estimate emissions accurately. It is essential to continuously update and refine emission inventories as new data and industrial activities emerge.

question_name: Identify and describe the most significant factors impacting on your jurisdiction’s ability to adapt to climate change and indicate how those factors either support or challenge this ability.
column_name: Describe how the factor supports or challenges the adaptive capacity of your jurisdiction^
response_answer: Access to healthcare plays a critical role in Can Tho City's ability to adapt to climate change. The impact of access to healthcare on the city's ability to adapt to climate change can either support or challenge its adaptation efforts, but the challenge is predominant as shown below:- Healthcare infrastructure and resources: Insufficient healthcare infrastructure, including medical facilities, hospitals, and health centers, can limit access to healthcare services, especially in remote or vulnerable areas. Inadequate resources, equipment, and healthcare personnel can pose challenges in responding to climate-related health emergencies and addressing the increased demand for healthcare services.- Vulnerable populations: Certain population groups, such as the elderly, children, pregnant women, and marginalized communities, may face greater health risks due to climate change. Limited access to healthcare services, socioeconomic disparities, and inadequate healthcare coverage can further exacerbate health vulnerabilities and hinder adaptation efforts.- Changing disease patterns: Climate change can contribute to shifts in disease patterns, emergence of new diseases, and increased prevalence of certain health conditions. These changes can challenge healthcare systems that may not be adequately prepared to address unfamiliar diseases or changing health burdens, leading to increased strain on healthcare resources.

response_answer: In the future, New Taipei City will invest  in its green budget every year to stimulate private green investment and green employment opportunities at the same time. In addition, the "New Taipei Climate Fund" will be set up in the future, with the carbon fee collected by the Environmental Protection Administration and voluntary donations from enterprises as the main source of income for the applications by communities, enterprises, households and schools, in order to promote the improvement of equipment energy efficiency, renewable energy installation and energy transformation. The City will also apply for international carbon certification for the carbon reduction quota of policy measures to assist the city government and enterprises to jointly achieve the carbon neutrality goal.In addition, the New Taipei  City will integrate the resources of the central government to promote the implementation of the "Green Finance Action Plan 2.0", leveraging green funds from the private sector from eight aspects, including credit extension, investment, capital market financing, talent cultivation, promotion of the deepening development of green financial products or services, information disclosure, prudential supervision, international linkage and incentive mechanism, to expand the scale of sustainable finance, and give priority to the completion of the inventory taking and verification of greenhouse gases of listed and OTC companies. Besides, the City will assist SMEs to promote the introduction of "Environment, Social and Governance" (ESG) sustainable management indicators, establish an information platform to integrate resources from all walks of life, establish and provide one stop consulting services, and guide enterprises in capacity building , such as carbon inventory taking, information disclosure and green production management.

question_name: Report details on the climate action plan or strategy that addresses mitigation, adaptation (resilience), and/or energy-related issues in your jurisdiction.
column_name: Describe if and how climate-related scenarios have informed the plan
response_answer: Climate-related scenarios have played a significant role in informing the implementation plan of the Paris Agreement on climate change in Can Tho City. These scenarios provide critical insights into the potential impacts of climate change and help identify areas of vulnerability and risk within the city.By incorporating climate-related scenarios into the implementation plan, Can Tho City assessed the potential future climate conditions, such as changes in temperature, precipitation patterns, sea-level rise, and extreme weather events. This analysis allowed the city to understand the specific challenges it may face and develop targeted strategies to address them.The climate-related scenarios helped Can Tho City identify priority areas for action and guide decision-making processes in setting mitigation goals. They assist in determining the necessary measures to reduce GHG emissions and enhance the city's resilience to climate change impacts.Based on these scenarios, the implementation plan may outline specific actions and strategies, such as promoting renewable energy sources, improving energy efficiency, implementing sustainable transportation systems, enhancing water management practices, etc. Furthermore, climate-related scenarios provide a foundation for monitoring and evaluating the progress of the implementation plan. By regularly assessing the city's climate-related risks and comparing them with the projected scenarios, Can Tho City can make adjustments and refine its strategies to ensure their effectiveness.

question_name: Report on your engagement with other levels of government regarding your jurisdiction's climate action.
response_answer: Indonesia is committed to reducing its GHG emissions by 41% by 2030 conditionally. The local government, including Medan City, must support this commitment and help achieve this goal. in Medan City Climate Action plan, There are two main focus that are climate mitigation and adaptation plan. The calculation indicates that Medan City's emission reduction goal for the year 2030 is 27.833%. Since the transportation industry makes up the majority of the emissions in Medan City, it is expected that more mitigation measures will be carried out. One of them is the use of rail-based mass transportation such as LRT, MRT, and KRL. Considering Medan City already has a railway line that has been idle for a while, this action will be accomplished. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct a feasibility study related to the reactivation of the rail line for the provision of mass transportation within Medan City.To lessen the effects of climate change that have already occurred or may occur in the future, adaptation to climate change must also be done in addition to mitigating activities. According to the findings of the urgency analysis study, there are currently 49 sub-districts that fall under the category of Urgency 1. In order for the sub-districts to be more resilient in the face of climate change, it is necessary to foresee this condition. The Medan City Government has taken and will continue to take steps to mitigate the effects of climate change, including improving drainage channels, building retention ponds, and building tidal flood retaining embankments.

response_answer: According to the "Taiwan’s Pathway to Net-Zero Emissions in 2050" issued by the National Development Council of the Executive Yuan in 2022, it is planned that 60~70% of the total electricity in 2050 will be renewable energy, 9~12% hydrogen energy, and 20~27% thermal power generation in consideration of energy security coupled with carbon capture, so as to achieve the decarbonization of the overall power supply. The implementation direction is divided into short-term and long-term stages as described below:1. Short-term (~ 2030)Energy system carbon reduction:Through energy transformation, increase green energy and give priority to mature wind power and optoelectronics, and deploy geothermal and marine energy technology research and development; increase natural gas to reduce the use of coal.2. Long-term (~ 2050)(1) Energy system:Maximize the deployment of renewable energy, and build a zero carbon power system through gas-fired power together with carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUs)  technology and the introduction of hydrogen power generation.(2) Maximizing the electrification of various industrial sectors and household appliances:Reduce non-electric carbon emissions and increase the proportion of zero-carbon energy in the power sector.(3) Various technology development:Actively invest in technology research and development, including wind power and photovoltaic power generation technologies, carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUs), and hydrogen power generation and application technology.Besides, New Taipei City has been cooperating with the central government in developing various renewable energy within its jurisdiction and currently, they are establishing the sulfur-Ziping geothermal demonstration area in Jinshan District.The city government has also assisted animal husbandry in setting up biogas power generation facilities, helped schools, communities and public buildings install solar panels on their roofs, and built three hydrogen power generation facilities to serve as backup power for disasters in rural areas. Three incineration plants within the jurisdiction are being renovated to improve incineration efficiency, and Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) technology is being introduced at one of the plants. New Taipei City is also planning to build a Biomass Energy Center to generate biogas from anaerobic fermentation as well as to treat citizen food waste.

response_answer: To consistently upgrade the air quality in Taoyuan City, the City government team is actively promoting the mobile pollution source reduction and low-pollution transport promotion measures to reduce the high-pollution potential motorcycles in Taoyuan City. In 2022, only 23,000 two-stroke motorcycles remained running, the ratio is 1.8%, which is the lowest ratio among the six metropolises in Taiwan; and the number of Phase 1 to 4 old motorcycles left are only 234,000, the ratio is 17.8%, which is also the lowest ratio among the six metropolises in Taiwan. The number of available electric facility charges (battery replace) stations have reached 1,789, which is the top one in Taiwan. Taoyuan City fully dedicated to implement and promote the air pollution control measures, continuously improving the air quality. In 2022, the proportion of days with good air quality (AQI≦50) has reached 70.6%, which is the highest one among the six metropolises, the fine suspended particulates (PM2.5) have dropped to 10.8μg/m3, which is a record low, and has been lower than the national air quality standard (15μg/m3) for 3 consecutive years.

response_answer: In response to international climate change and global warming trends, New Taipei City has been promoting climate change adaptation and mitigation for a long time. In 2007, it established the "Low-Carbon Community Development Centre" under the Environmental Protection Agency which became the first local government in Taiwan to set up an independent unit to implement carbon reduction work. In 2016, the city government established the "Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation Promotion Team" across agencies, with 17 agencies working together to address climate change and discuss greenhouse gas reduction measures.The City actively promotes climate change mitigation and adaptation. In 2020, a "New Taipei City Climate Action Plan" was specially compiled, which divides mitigation work into the sectors of renewable energy, industrial energy conservation, energy-efficient buildings, energy conservation, green transportation, and sustainable agriculture and forestry for implementation of the action plan. For the adaptation work, corresponding strategies for the impact of climate change are formulated according to various fields, and care visits for the homeless and the elderly living alone are carried out for the climate-vulnerable groups, cold weather protection materials are provided, and resettlement is encouraged and arranged when the temperature drops sharply, so as to protect the lives of homeless and elderly people living alone.

question_name: Provide details on your climate risk and vulnerability assessment.
response_answer: The level of potential impact in a region is determined using SIDIK, which is the result of calculations based on indicators of potential impact, namely exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity of neighborhoods. Sensitivity represents the internal conditions of a system (in this report, focused on neighborhood systems) indicating the degree of vulnerability to disruptions caused by disasters. Adaptive capacity, on the other hand, represents a system's ability to adjust to climate change, which involves long-term adjustments to hazardous events like disasters. Sensitivity and adaptive capacity data represent indicators of vulnerability. The third factor determining potential impact is exposure, which shows the condition and level of a system's exposure to environmental disturbances such as climate-related disasters. The combination of vulnerability and exposure results in the potential impact index.The indicators of sensitivity, adaptive capacity, and exposure used to determine the level of potential impact in Medan are presented in Table 4. Brief descriptions for each sensitivity and adaptive capacity indicator are provided in Appendices 1 and 2.Table 4-1: Indicators of Adaptive Capacity, Exposure, and Sensitivity (IKS) in Determining the Level of Potential Impact (Neighborhoods) in Medan CityCategory Indicator Description Related TPBs (SDGs)Exposure IndicatorsKE 1 Population to Area Ratio TPB 11KE 2 Building to Area Ratio TPB 11KE 3 House Building Ratio TPB 11Sensitivity IndicatorsSE1 Dependency Population Ratio TPB 2SE2 Households with Sanitation Facilities Ratio TPB 6SE3 Poor Population or Household Ratio TPB 1SE4 Unemployed Population Ratio TPB 8SE5 Population and Slum Settlement Buildings Ratio TPB 11SE6 Population and Buildings on Riverbanks Ratio TPB 11Adaptive Capacity IndicatorsKA1 Population Ratio based on Education & School Participation Rate TPB 4KA2 Population Ratio based on Occupation TPB 8KA3 Health Facilities Ratio to Population TPB 3KA4 Small Industries Ratio to Population TPB 8KA5 Economic Centers Ratio to Population TPB 8KA6 Green Open Spaces Number TPB 11KA7 Social Institutions Ratio to Population TPB 16KA8 Banking Facilities Ratio to Population TPB 8Neighborhoods with high potential impact levels are due to high exposure and sensitivity to disturbances and disasters, but without sufficient adaptive capacity to address the impacts. One effort to reduce the potential impact level is the development of adaptation actions, which can be integrated with development programs and activities. Successful adaptation actions can be seen from their impact on various development aspects.Therefore, the neighborhood's potential impact indicators in Table 4-1 are grouped based on national development aspects aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The results of grouping the 17 neighborhood potential impact indicators (KA, SE, and KE) based on development aspects can be seen in Table 4-2. A more detailed description of the reasons for this grouping can be found in Appendices 1 and 2.Table 4-2: Grouping of Vulnerability Indicators based on Sustainable Development Goal AspectsDevelopment Aspect Symbol Vulnerability IndicatorsEducation KA1 Education LevelHealth KA3 Health FacilitiesEcosystem KE1 Population to Area Ratio (Population Density)KE2 Building to Area RatioKA6 Green Open Spaces NumberPoverty Reduction SE1 Dependency Population RatioSE3 Poor Population or Household RatioSE4 Unemployed Population RatioSE5 Population and Slum Settlement Buildings RatioSE6 Population and Buildings on Riverbanks RatioInfrastructure KE3 House Building RatioSE2 Households with Sanitation Facilities RatioEconomy/Livelihood KA2 Population Ratio based on OccupationKA4 Small Industries Ratio to PopulationKA5 Economic Centers Ratio to PopulationKA8 Banking Facilities Ratio to PopulationGovernance KA7 Social Institutions Ratio to Population4.3. Level of Neighborhood Potential ImpactThe level of potential impact in neighborhoods in Medan City varies greatly, ranging from very low to very high (Table 4-5). According to Table 4-5, the majority of neighborhoods in Medan City fall into the categories of very low, low, and moderately low potential impact. However, there are also 5 neighborhoods classified as having a very high potential impact level, namely Mangga, Beringin, Tanjung Sari, Tanjung Gusta, and Bandar Selamat. The spatial distribution of the neighborhood's potential impact levels in Medan City is obtained using the Vulnerability Index Data Information System (SIDIK).

response_answer: Ce bassin fait partie de la plaine côtière du Cameroun. C’est un milieu naturel spécifique à écologie fragile caractérisé par la présence de mangroves, de la forêt atlantique avec une biodiversité riche (faune et flore). Au gré de diverses contingences, le Bassin est désormais au cœur de multiples pressions qui induisent sa dégradation et formulent des préoccupations quant à la sauvegarde des écosystèmes naturels et de la biodiversité qu’il abrite. Les moteurs de cette dynamique dégradante agrègent à la fois, l’urbanisation galopante dans la partie Est de Douala, les pollutions industrielles, l’essor de l’extraction de sable dans le lit du fleuve, l’intensification de la pêche artisanale ; mais aussi le développement des activités agricoles à l’intérieur de la plaine alluviale voire globalement du bassin versant du fleuve.Face à pression urbaine et démographique susmentionnées, ces problèmes s’avèrent prégnants et exigent, dans une perspective de sauvegarde de ce bassin et de sa biodiversité, un regard holistique impliquant un panel de divers spécialistes. La question est d’autant plus actuelle que les enjeux de développement durable interpellent la gouvernance des villes avec l’émergence des concepts comme « villes durables », « villes vertes », etc. qui renouvellent les modalités d’intégration/réintégration de la nature au sein des villes. Nature artificialisée le plus souvent, mais de plus en plus exigence de sauvegarde et d’incorporation des espaces naturels au sein (ou à la lisière) des villes. Il faut dire que les préoccupations sur les changements climatiques sont passées par là et impliquent désormais un réexamen profond de la conception et de la planification urbaine avec une emphase sur les espaces verts. La question fondamentale est celle de savoir comment sauvegarder et conserver les écosystèmes naturels, la biodiversité et le patrimoine culturel dans le bassin de la Dibamba en contexte de développement de la ville de Douala ? Comment parvenir à une urbanisation durable de Douala dans le secteur de la Dibamba ?ACTIVITESA.1. Sauvegarde de l’écosystème fluvial de la Dibamba∙ Revue documentaire, Information, sensibilisation des parties prenantes ; ∙ Enquêtes socio-foncières ∙ Sessions des organes de suivi ∙ Atelier de validation du cadrage ∙ Cadrage socio-environnemental A.2 Valorisation des ressources du fleuve Dibamba∙ Montage des dossiers et plaidoyers auprès des partenaires potentiels de ONU-Habitat A.3 Création d’un Laboratoire de Gouvernance Territoriale∙ Revue du document Douala Métropolitain Observatory et finalisation des aspects financiers à compléter ∙ Etude de faisabilité de la mise sur pied d'un observatoire au sein de la commune de Dicamba ∙ Montage financier ∙ Conception d'un réseau d'observations et de collecte des données ∙ Développement des plateformes et des applications mobiles ∙ Création d'une plateforme d'interopérabilité et fédératrice des observatoires dans la ville de Douala ∙ Renforcement des capacités du personnel A.4. Suivi-Evaluation de la mise en œuvre des activités du projet∙ Mise sur pied d'un organisme de gestion intégrée du bassin versant de la rivière Dibamba (OGIBR) ∙ Fonctionnement de l'organisme ∙ Développement du POS le long des berges de la Rivière Dibamba ∙ Autres documents de planification urbaine et stratégique ∙ Campagne de communication / sensibilisation à travers les médias à l'attention des riverains sur l'importance l'organisme de gestion intégrée du bassin versant ∙ Création d'une structure intercommunale ∙ A.5.
